6. Short term loans and overdrafts  
 
ADs may obtain short term loans and overdrafts for a period not exceeding seven days at a time 
from overseas branches and correspondents at the going market rates to meet their short term 
needs. If these loans or overdrafts require collateral in Bangladesh or abroad prior approval must 
be obtained from Bangladesh Bank. Short term loans and overdrafts taken under the authority of 
this paragraph may be remitted by ADs without prior approval of Bangladesh Bank, but subject 
to report.  
 
7. Reconciliation of nostro accounts  
 
In pursuance to the 'Foreign Exchange Risk Management Guidelines' (as prescribed by FE 
Circular Letter No. 12, dated February 20, 2025 and subsequent amendments) to be followed in 
case of foreign exchange risks for reconciliation of nostro accounts, Head Offices/Principle 
Offices of ADs are required to submit comprehensive review of all nostro accounts containing a 
complete list of all un-reconciled entries at the end of each quarter of the year; the list to be 
prepared by officials who have no involvement in the transaction and approval process of the 
nostro accounts. Banks are also required to make provisions periodically for debit entries 
remaining un-reconciled for more than six months as per schedule issued by Bangladesh Bank 
from time to time. In addition, June and December end reviews must be accompanied with 
certification of the External Auditor of the bank concerned on correctness of the status of the un-
reconciled entries mentioned on the review.  
 
Besides, banks are also required to submit summary of un-reconciled nostro account entries at 
the end of each month through online web portal (paragraph 26, chapter 2 of GFET-2). However, 
quarter-end statement will include summary of un-reconciled entries as per format given in 
Appendix 50, GFET, Vol-2.

prepared by officials who have no involvement in the transaction and approval process of the 
nostro accounts. Banks are also required to make provisions periodically for debit entries 
remaining un-reconciled for more than six months as per schedule issued by Bangladesh Bank 
from time to time. In addition, June and December end reviews must be accompanied with 
certification of the External Auditor of the bank concerned on correctness of the status of the un-
reconciled entries mentioned on the review.  
 
Besides, banks are also required to submit summary of un-reconciled nostro account entries at 
the end of each month through online web portal (paragraph 26, chapter 2 of GFET-2). However, 
quarter-end statement will include summary of un-reconciled entries as per format given in 
Appendix 50, GFET, Vol-2.

6. Short term loans and overdrafts  
 
ADs may obtain short term loans and overdrafts for a period not exceeding seven days at a time 
from overseas branches and correspondents at the going market rates to meet their short term 
needs. If these loans or overdrafts require collateral in Bangladesh or abroad prior approval must 
be obtained from Bangladesh Bank. Short term loans and overdrafts taken under the authority of 
this paragraph may be remitted by ADs without prior approval of Bangladesh Bank, but subject 
to report.  
 
7. Reconciliation of nostro accounts  
 
In pursuance to the 'Foreign Exchange Risk Management Guidelines' (as prescribed by FE 
Circular Letter No. 12, dated February 20, 2025 and subsequent amendments) to be followed in 
case of foreign exchange risks for reconciliation of nostro accounts, Head Offices/Principle 
Offices of ADs are required to submit comprehensive review of all nostro accounts containing a 
complete list of all un-reconciled entries at the end of each quarter of the year; the list to be 
prepared by officials who have no involvement in the transaction and approval process of the 
nostro accounts. Banks are also required to make provisions periodically for debit entries 
remaining un-reconciled for more than six months as per schedule issued by Bangladesh Bank 
from time to time. In addition, June and December end reviews must be accompanied with 
certification of the External Auditor of the bank concerned on correctness of the status of the un-
reconciled entries mentioned on the review.  
 
Besides, banks are also required to submit summary of un-reconciled nostro account entries at 
the end of each month through online web portal (paragraph 26, chapter 2 of GFET-2). However, 
quarter-end statement will include summary of un-reconciled entries as per format given in 
Appendix 50, GFET, Vol-2.

Part-F 
FORWARD DEALINGS IN FOREIGN EXCHANGE 
1. General  
 
ADs may engage in forward sales only against bona fide need of the customers/counterparty 
banks. In all cases, ADs must ensure that the cover is intended to neutralize the risks arising from 
such transactions. ADs may purchase forward from banks and non-bank customers like 
exporters, foreign currency account holders including retention quota accounts of exporters, 
foreign currency accounts of specialized zones (export processing industrial areas such as EPZ, 
HTP, EPA of Invest Bangladesh Authority), exchange houses abroad etc. Be it forward sale or 
purchase, ADs must cover their own risk within the shortest possible time. 
 
2. Forward sale and purchase  
 
(a) All forward contracts should be treated as firm and should be closed out on expiry. In such 
cases, ADs should charge the difference between the contracted (booked) rate and the TT clean 
spot buying or TT spot selling rate, as the case may be, ruling on the date the contract is closed 
out. The forward contract should be closed without charging any difference if the rate moves in 
favor of the customer on the date of the closure. In other words, in case of a forward purchase by 
an AD no difference will be charged if the TT spot selling rate on the date of closure is at par or 
lower (i.e., inferior from the point of view of the customer) than the booked rate. Similarly, no 
difference should be charged for closing out a forward sale contract if the TT clean spot buying 
rate on the date of closure is at par or higher (i.e., costlier than the booked rate from the point of 
view of the customer) than the booked rate. 
 
(b) With a view to bringing operational flexibility, forward contracts may be renewed/rolled 
over/extended for the new delivery period at the prevailing market rate, provided ADs are 
satisfied with documentary evidences that customers are unable to perform the contracts due to 
changes in the actual requirements or other valid exigencies. In such cases, when both the 
cancellation and re-booking of forward contracts are undertaken simultaneously, gain to 
customers, if any thereon, to be passed on to customers at the time of entering into new 
arrangement. Such gains favoring customers shall be retained in margin accounts of customers 
till the close of the underlying transactions. Balances held in this account may be utilized by ADs 
for realizing dues from the customers for this purpose.    
 
(c) Forward contracts may be executed on outright full settlement or net settlement on non-
deliverable basis in conformity with the principle of satisfying bona fide needs of the resident 
business entities. Hence, it is permissible to book short term non-deliverable forward contracts 
with roll-over flexibility till maturity for ultimate settlement on deliverable basis against 
underlying transactions having long tenor. In the context of settlement of gain/loss in favor of 
customers during the split tenor of the contracts, the procedure as stated above shall apply.

(ii) With regard to forward buying rate, ADs shall consider spot buying rate to calculate the 
desired rate on adjustment of forward premium. 
 
3. Swap Transactions  
 
ADs may undertake swap transactions in line with their counterparty limit in accordance with the 
core risk management guidelines issued by Bangladesh Bank to cover their risks arising from 
forward transactions and manage cash flow mismatch arising out of day to day transactions. 
However, they are advised to refrain from taking speculative positions through swap 
transactions. 
 
4. Cross currency forward and swap  
 
Cross currency swap and forward, not backed by underlying customers' transactions, can be 
undertaken only if the 'Foreign Exchange Risk Management Guidelines' (as prescribed by FE 
Circular Letter No. 12, dated February 20, 2025 and subsequent amendments) are implemented 
to the satisfaction of Bangladesh Bank. 
 
5. Keeping records and submission of statements  
 
All documents (copy of LCs, contracts etc.) relating to forward contracts and swap transactions 
must be preserved for subsequent inspection by Bangladesh Bank. Besides, ADs shall report all 
the interbank transactions on daily basis through online as instructed in paragraph 26, chapter 2 
of GFET (Vol-2).  
 
6. Two way quotation  
 
ADs are advised to quote both sale and purchase rate while quoting/asking for any spot/forward 
transaction in the interbank market.

HEDGING OF COMMODITY PRICE RISK FOR  
IMPORT TRADES IN INTERNATIONAL MARKETS 
 
ADs are permitted to facilitate and offer commodity price risk hedging products to eligible 
importers, irrespective of whether such importers operate within designated specialized zones or 
outside such zones, within a structured, transparent, and supervised framework, subject to the 
terms and conditions set out in FEPD-1 Circular No. 34, dated September 13, 2026 (Enclosure-
A).

Part-H 
PROHIBITION REGARDING VIRTUAL ASSETS, VIRTUAL CURRENCIES  
AND FACILITATING THEIR EXCHANGE/TRANSFER/TRADING 
 
 
Foreign Exchange Policy Department of Bangladesh Bank (now Foreign Exchange Policy 
Department-2) has imposed restriction on virtual assets and virtual currencies, including 
activities facilitating their exchange, transfer or trading vide FE Circular No. 24, dated 
September 15, 2022 (Enclosure-B). Similar prohibitions were subsequently reiterated through 
BRPD Circular Letter No. 40, dated October 12, 2022 and DFIM Circular Letter No. 24, 
November 10, 2022 (Enclosure-C and D) addressed to all scheduled banks, and financial 
institutions. The restrictions remain in force, and the concerned parties are required to comply 
with the applicable instructions issued by Bangladesh Bank.

FEPD-1 Circular No. 34                                                            Date: September 13, 2026 
All Authorized Dealers in  
Foreign Exchange in Bangladesh 
Hedging of Commodity Price Risk for Import Trades in International Markets 
 Dear Sirs, 
In view of the evolving dynamics of global commodity markets, which highlight 
the importance of effective price risk management for importers in Bangladesh, the 
adoption of appropriate risk management practices may facilitate better cost planning 
and enhance business competitiveness.  
02. Bangladesh Bank, in exercise of the powers conferred under Section 20(3) of 
the Foreign Exchange Regulation (FER) Act, 1947, hereby issues enclosed the 
Guidelines on Hedging of Commodity Price Risk for import trades in international 
markets to promote prudent risk management practices and align with international 
standards.  
03. Authorized Dealers (ADs) are permitted to facilitate and offer commodity 
price risk hedging products to eligible importers, irrespective of whether such importers 
operate within designated specialized zones or outside such zones, within a structured, 
transparent, and supervised framework, subject to the terms and conditions set out in 
these guidelines. 
04. In light of the above decision, the instructions contained at paragraph 14, 
chapter 4 of the Guidelines for Foreign Exchange Transactions (GFET)-2018, Vol-1, 
shall stand amended.  
Please bring the contents of this circular to the notice of all concerned.  
  
 
 
Yours faithfully, 
Encl. As stated.                                                                        
 
 (Dr. Md. Abu Bakkar Siddique) 
Director (FEPD-1) (Current Charge) 
Phone: 9530092

1 
 
 
Guidelines on 
Hedging of Commodity Price Risk for Import Trades in International Markets 
In exercise of the powers conferred under Section 20(3) of the FER Act, 1947, 
Bangladesh Bank hereby issues the following Guidelines. 
1. Short title 
These instructions shall be known as the Guidelines on Hedging of Commodity Price 
Risk for Import Trades in International Markets, 2026. These instructions shall come 
into force with immediate effect. 
2. Definitions 
(a) Exposure to commodity price risk 
“Exposure to Commodity Price Risk” means any direct or indirect exposure to 
fluctuations in commodity prices arising from import transactions in international 
markets. 
(i) Direct exposure – An importer shall be deemed to have direct exposure where 
the imported commodity, or any component thereof, is priced based on an 
internationally recognized benchmark. 
(ii) Indirect exposure – An importer shall be deemed to have indirect exposure 
where the imported product contains a commodity that is not explicitly benchmark-
linked but whose price remains subject to price. 
(b) Hedging – “Hedging” means the activity of entering into a derivative transaction to 
mitigate an identifiable and measurable commodity price risk. 
(c) Eligible importers – “Eligible Importers” means importers who meet the criteria set 
out in paragraph 3 of these guidelines. 
(d) Hedge classification – 
(i) Procurement hedge – A hedge undertaken prior to import or purchase in order 
to manage the risk of an increase in commodity price. 
(ii) Structured hedge – A hedge undertaken by using a combination of permitted 
hedging instruments in order to improve cost efficiency or define a price band, 
without creating net open speculative exposure. 
3. Eligible importers 
Eligibility shall be established on the basis of verifiable underlying exposure supported 
by confirmed import orders, letters of credit, or purchase agreements denominated in 
foreign currency. Eligible importers include:

4 
 
(r) Where necessary for effective risk mitigation, ADs may facilitate associated foreign 
exchange transactions in accordance with existing regulations; 
(s) ADs shall ensure that importers are made aware of potential mark-to-market, 
premium, margin, settlement, and contingent liability implications before execution of 
any hedging transaction. 
6. Hedge limits 
Importers may hedge up to 100 percent of their underlying commodity exposure, 
including partial coverage where appropriate. Multiple hedge contracts may be executed 
provided the aggregate value does not exceed the import exposure. ADs shall ensure 
that each hedge is closely matched in terms of timing, quantity, and contract 
specifications with the underlying transaction, as the case may be. 
7. Prudential and documentation requirements 
(a) Importers shall maintain detailed records of each hedging transaction including: 
(i) Contract details: notional amount, maturity, strike price, settlement terms; 
benchmark, and premium where applicable; 
(ii) Evidence of corresponding import exposure; 
(iii) Hedge classification as procurement hedge and/or structured hedge; 
(iv) Internal approvals and risk management policy references. 
(b) Importers shall submit to ADs a written declaration confirming that the hedge has 
been undertaken solely for risk mitigation and not for speculative gain. 
(c) ADs shall retain all related records for inspection by Bangladesh Bank and for 
compliance with prudential supervision. 
(d) ADs shall ensure that hedge effectiveness is demonstrable through price correlation, 
economic offset or other appropriate internal methodology. 
8. Accounting and valuation 
(a) Hedging gains or losses shall be accounted for in accordance with International 
Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS-9), where applicable. 
(b) Hedging gains or losses shall be properly recognized in financial statements in line 
with the matched exposure principle in the importer’s financial statements. 
(c) Importers are responsible for accounting treatment in their financial statements 
consistent with applicable local regulations and auditing requirements.

document_pages.native_text:
4 
 
(r) Where necessary for effective risk mitigation, ADs may facilitate associated foreign 
exchange transactions in accordance with existing regulations; 
(s) ADs shall ensure that importers are made aware of potential mark-to-market, 
premium, margin, settlement, and contingent liability implications before execution of 
any hedging transaction. 
6. Hedge limits 
Importers may hedge up to 100 percent of their underlying commodity exposure, 
including partial coverage where appropriate. Multiple hedge contracts may be executed 
provided the aggregate value does not exceed the import exposure. ADs shall ensure 
that each hedge is closely matched in terms of timing, quantity, and contract 
specifications with the underlying transaction, as the case may be. 
7. Prudential and documentation requirements 
(a) Importers shall maintain detailed records of each hedging transaction including: 
(i) Contract details: notional amount, maturity, strike price, settlement terms; 
benchmark, and premium where applicable; 
(ii) Evidence of corresponding import exposure; 
(iii) Hedge classification as procurement hedge and/or structured hedge; 
(iv) Internal approvals and risk management policy references. 
(b) Importers shall submit to ADs a written declaration confirming that the hedge has 
been undertaken solely for risk mitigation and not for speculative gain. 
(c) ADs shall retain all related records for inspection by Bangladesh Bank and for 
compliance with prudential supervision. 
(d) ADs shall ensure that hedge effectiveness is demonstrable through price correlation, 
economic offset or other appropriate internal methodology. 
8. Accounting and valuation 
(a) Hedging gains or losses shall be accounted for in accordance with International 
Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS-9), where applicable. 
(b) Hedging gains or losses shall be properly recognized in financial statements in line 
with the matched exposure principle in the importer’s financial statements. 
(c) Importers are responsible for accounting treatment in their financial statements 
consistent with applicable local regulations and auditing requirements.

5 
 
9. Supervisory and reporting arrangements 
(a) ADs shall report all importer-linked hedging transactions to Bangladesh Bank on a 
monthly basis as per Annexure I, detailing commodity type, hedge classification, 
instrument, amount, maturity, and counterparties. 
(b) Any irregularity, default, speculative use or misuse of these instructions will be 
reported immediately to Bangladesh Bank. 
(c) Non-compliance may result in suspension of hedging facility or other regulatory 
actions. 
10. Risk awareness 
ADs shall advise importers that hedging is a risk-management tool and not a profit-
generating mechanism. It reduces uncertainty but cannot eliminate market risk. Adverse 
price movements opposite to the hedged position may result in losses. Importers shall, 
therefore, fully understand product features, premium, margin requirements, potential 
mark-to-market obligations, contingent liabilities under written options, and settlement 
procedures before entering into any contract. 
11. Internal systems and controls 
ADs shall align their internal risk management systems, due diligence procedures and 
control mechanisms with best international standards for commodity derivative 
transactions. 
12. Client accommodation 
ADs shall accommodate importers' hedging requests upon receipt of the required 
documentation, along with importers' internal approvals. 
13. Periodic return  
ADs shall submit a quarterly report to Foreign Exchange Policy Department-1, 
Bangladesh Bank, in the prescribed format (Annexure II). In case of no transactions, a 
“Nil” report shall be submitted. 
14. Prior concurrence of Bangladesh Bank 
ADs intending to offer commodity price hedging services under this circular shall

procedures (SOP).

Schedule I 
Commodity Futures  
Description: 
Commodity futures are standardized contracts traded on exchanges that enable 
importers to lock in a future price for a commodity. To manage the risk of price 
fluctuations between the contract date and the shipment or payment date, the importer or 
its bank takes a futures position. 
Operational flow: 
(a) Importer signs commodity purchase contract with exporter. 
(b) Importer requests LC from a Bangladeshi commercial bank, where applicable. 
(c) AD bank issues the LC through international banking networks. 
(d) Importer requests price hedging through the AD bank. 
(e) AD bank executes a futures contract through an international broker or exchange 
member. 
(f) Futures position is held until shipment or price exposure period ends. 
(g) Gains or losses from futures offset commodity price movement.

Description: 
A commodity forward contract is a customized agreement between two parties to buy or 
sell a commodity at a predetermined price on a specific future date. Unlike futures 
contracts, which are standardized and traded on exchanges, forwards are typically 
traded over-the-counter (OTC) through banks and are tailored to meet the specific needs 
of the importer. 
Operational flow: 
(a) Importer signs commodity purchase agreement with the supplier. 
(b) Importer asks the AD bank to lock the future commodity price. 
(c) AD Bank quotes forward price. 
(d) Forward contract is agreed. 
(e) AD Bank offsets risk in the international market, where applicable. 
(f) Importer financing and LC opening (optional). 
(g) Commodity delivery and forward contract settlement take place on the agreed 
date

current market price is USD 360 per ton. To manage future price fluctuations, the 
importer has entered into a forward contract with a bank at a price of USD 365 per ton.

purchase the wheat for the agreed price of USD 365 under the forward contract, 
thereby avoiding the higher market price. 
 If the market price falls to USD 330 per ton, the importer is still obligated to buy

allow the importer to benefit from price decreases.

document_pages.raw_text:
14 
 
Schedule IV 
Commodity Options  
Description: 
Commodity options provide price protection. The importer purchases the right, but not 
the obligation, to buy or sell the commodity at a predetermined strike price. To obtain 
this protection, the importer pays an option premium except where the structure has 
been arranged on a zero-cost basis through a permitted collar strategy. 
Types of Option-Based Hedging Structures: 
(a) Procurement hedge using call option 
A call option may be used by an importer to hedge against an increase in commodity 
prices prior to procurement. This enables the importer to secure a maximum purchase 
price while retaining the benefit of any price decline. 
(b) Zero-Cost collar structure 
A collar structure involves the simultaneous purchase of a call option and sale of a put 
option, or such other permitted combination of option legs, in order to reduce or 
eliminate upfront premium cost. The structure shall be constructed such that it provides 
a defined price band and does not result in speculative exposure. 
Operational flow: 
(a) Importer signs commodity supply contract. 
(b) Importer opens LC with issuing bank, where applicable. 
(c) Importer requests a call option, put option, or collar structure through the AD 
bank depending on the nature of exposure. 
(d) AD bank executes the option transaction through an international derivatives 
broker, exchange, or bank counterparty. 
(e) If market price moves adversely (increase), the option payoff offsets the increase 
in procurement cost, as the case may be. 
(f) If market prices move favorably (decrease), the importer may benefit from 
market movement subject to the premium paid or collar range agreed.

Example 1: Procurement hedge using call option 
An importer plans to purchase crude oil in three months. Current market price: USD 82 
per barrel. The importer purchases a call option with a strike price of USD 82 by paying 
a premium of USD 2. 
Outcome: 
 If the market price rises to USD 100 per barrel, the importer exercises the option 
and effectively caps the purchase price at USD 82. 
 If the market price falls to USD 70 per barrel, the importer purchases at market 
price and only incurs loss of the premium cost USD 2.

the call option, resulting in zero net premiums.

Managing Directors/CEOs

Foreign Exchange dealings in Bangladesh 
 
Dear Sirs, 
 
"Prohibition regarding virtual assets, virtual currencies and 
facilitating their exchange/transfer/trading  
 
Refer to Bangladesh Bank public notice no. DCP(PR)1/2021-7/5 dated July 29, 2021 where 
all persons and institutions concerned were repeatedly cautioned about various risks associated in 
dealing with virtual currencies/crypto currencies.  
 
 
2. The definition of “currency” given in section 2(b)(i) of the Foreign Exchange Regulation 
(FER) Act, 1947 does not recognize virtual currencies. Virtual currencies [subset of virtual assets] are 
neither approved foreign exchange/currency nor approved form of transactions/investments in 
accordance with section- 2(aa) and 2(bb) of the FER Act, 1947. Virtual currencies or virtual assets 
have no financial claim embedded and neither issued by any sovereign nor guaranteed by any 
jurisdiction. Thus, their value is highly volatile and associated with high financial risks. Nonetheless, 
borderless transactions of unregulated virtual currencies are growing fast and being exchanged with 
some other foreign currencies, thus treated as an alternative form of foreign exchange transactions 
which is contravention of the FER Act, 1947. 
 
 
3. The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) has defined virtual assets as a digital 
representation of value that can be digitally traded, or transferred, and can be used for payment or 
investment purposes. Point to be noted that, virtual assets do not include digital representations of fiat 
currencies, securities and other financial assets, recognized by Bangladesh Bank. 
 
4. Retention of export proceeds abroad in any form without limiting to equity/portfolio 
investment, purchase of physical assets/virtual assets, maintenance of accounts regardless of 
currencies including crypto currencies constitutes contravention of the FER Act, 1947 and is subject 
to cognizance under Section 23(1) of the said act as mentioned in FE Circular No. 39 of November 
18, 2021. Any transactions made in/from/to Bangladesh for obtaining virtual assets (as defined in 
paragraph 3) or its subset- virtual currencies, are not permitted by Bangladesh Bank. As well as 
Enclosure-B

1 
 
Foreign Exchange Policy Department 
Bangladesh Bank 
Head Office, Dhaka 
www.bb.org.bd 
 
 
FE Circular No. 24                               
 
 
 
 
    Date: September 15, 2022 
 
 
Managing Directors/CEOs 
All Scheduled Banks/ Authorized Dealers of Foreign Exchange 
/MFS Providers/Financial Institutions/Other Concerns and 
All stakeholders associated with 
Foreign Exchange dealings in Bangladesh 
 
Dear Sirs, 
 
"Prohibition regarding virtual assets, virtual currencies and 
facilitating their exchange/transfer/trading  
 
Refer to Bangladesh Bank public notice no. DCP(PR)1/2021-7/5 dated July 29, 2021 where 
all persons and institutions concerned were repeatedly cautioned about various risks associated in 
dealing with virtual currencies/crypto currencies.  
 
 
2. The definition of “currency” given in section 2(b)(i) of the Foreign Exchange Regulation 
(FER) Act, 1947 does not recognize virtual currencies. Virtual currencies [subset of virtual assets] are 
neither approved foreign exchange/currency nor approved form of transactions/investments in 
accordance with section- 2(aa) and 2(bb) of the FER Act, 1947. Virtual currencies or virtual assets 
have no financial claim embedded and neither issued by any sovereign nor guaranteed by any 
jurisdiction. Thus, their value is highly volatile and associated with high financial risks. Nonetheless, 
borderless transactions of unregulated virtual currencies are growing fast and being exchanged with 
some other foreign currencies, thus treated as an alternative form of foreign exchange transactions 
which is contravention of the FER Act, 1947. 
 
 
3. The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) has defined virtual assets as a digital 
representation of value that can be digitally traded, or transferred, and can be used for payment or 
investment purposes. Point to be noted that, virtual assets do not include digital representations of fiat 
currencies, securities and other financial assets, recognized by Bangladesh Bank. 
 
4. Retention of export proceeds abroad in any form without limiting to equity/portfolio 
investment, purchase of physical assets/virtual assets, maintenance of accounts regardless of 
currencies including crypto currencies constitutes contravention of the FER Act, 1947 and is subject 
to cognizance under Section 23(1) of the said act as mentioned in FE Circular No. 39 of November 
18, 2021. Any transactions made in/from/to Bangladesh for obtaining virtual assets (as defined in 
paragraph 3) or its subset- virtual currencies, are not permitted by Bangladesh Bank. As well as 
Enclosure-B

document_pages.raw_text:
2 
 
providing any kind of facilitation in favor of doing business, activities, and operations associated with 
exchange/transfer/trading of virtual assets or virtual currencies, are not permitted by Bangladesh 
Bank. 
5. Any violation of the aforementioned instructions (as defined in paragraph 4) constitutes 
contravention of Section 5(1)(e) of the FER Act, 1947 and is subject to cognizance under Section 
23(1) of the said Act as per SRO No. 59-LAW/2021 dated March 08, 2021. Therefore, all 
individuals/entities/institutions operating in Bangladesh shall refrain from dealing in virtual assets, 
virtual currencies and providing any kind of facilitation in favor of doing business, activities, and 
operations associated with exchange/transfer/trading of virtual assets or virtual currencies. 
 
6. This circular is issued in exercise of the power conferred under section- 20(3) of the 
Foreign Exchange Regulation (FER) Act, 1947.   
Please bring the contents of this circular to the notice of your clientele for awareness on 
virtual assets. 
 
 
Yours faithfully, 
 
 
                                                                                                                 (Md. Sarwar Hossain)  
Director (FEPD)  
 
 
                                                                     Phone: 9530123

5. Any violation of the aforementioned instructions (as defined in paragraph 4) constitutes 
contravention of Section 5(1)(e) of the FER Act, 1947 and is subject to cognizance under Section 
23(1) of the said Act as per SRO No. 59-LAW/2021 dated March 08, 2021. Therefore, all 
individuals/entities/institutions operating in Bangladesh shall refrain from dealing in virtual assets, 
virtual currencies and providing any kind of facilitation in favor of doing business, activities, and 
operations associated with exchange/transfer/trading of virtual assets or virtual currencies. 
 
6. This circular is issued in exercise of the power conferred under section- 20(3) of the 
Foreign Exchange Regulation (FER) Act, 1947.   
Please bring the contents of this circular to the notice of your clientele for awareness on 
virtual assets.

বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংক
প্রধান কাযার্লয়
মতিঝিল, ঢাকা-১০০০
বাংলাদেশ।
বিনংরঃব: িি.িনন.ড়ৎম.নফ

ব্যাংকিং প্রবিধি ও নীতি বিভাগ

১২ অক্টোবর ২০২২
বিআরপিডি সাকুর্লার লেটার নং-৪০
তারিখ: -----------------

২৭ আশ্বিন ১৪২৯
ব্যবস্থাপনা পরিচালক/প্রধান নিবার্হী কমর্কতার্
বাংলাদেশে কাযর্রত সকল তফসিলি ব্যাংক

প্রিয় মহোদয়,
ভাচুর্য়াল সম্পদ (ঠরৎঃঁধষ ধংংবঃ) ও ভাচুর্য়াল মুদ্রা (ঠরৎঃঁধষ পঁৎৎবহপু) লেনদেন এবং তাদের
বিনিময়/স্থানান্ত্মর/বাণিজ্য (ঊীপযধহমব/ঞৎধহংভবৎ/ঞৎধফরহম) সংক্রান্ত্ম নিষেধাজ্ঞা প্রসঙ্গে।

শিরোনামোক্ত বিষয়ে ঙ্বদেশিক মুদ্রা নীতি বিভাগ কতৃর্ক ১৫ সেপ্টেম্বর ২০২২ তারিখে জারিকৃত এফই সাকুর্লার নং-২৪
এর প্রতি আপনাদের দৃষ্টি আকষর্ণ করা যাচ্ছে।
২। সূত্রোক্ত সাকুর্লারের মাধ্যমে ভাচুর্য়াল সম্পদ (ঠরৎঃঁধষ ধংংবঃ) ও ভাচুর্য়াল মুদ্রা (ঠরৎঃঁধষ পঁৎৎবহপু) লেনদেন এবং
তাদের বিনিময়/স্থানান্ত্মর/বাণিজ্যের (ঊীপযধহমব/ঞৎধহংভবৎ/ঞৎধফরহম) সাথে যুক্ত ব্যবসা ও এ সংক্রান্ত্ম যেকোন ধরনের কাযর্ক্রমে
সহায়তা প্রদান হতে বিরত থাকার জন্য নিদের্শনা দেওয়া হয়েছে। সম্প্রতি লক্ষ করা যাচ্ছে যে, বিভিন্ন বিদেশী ঠরৎঃঁধষ অংংবঃ
ঝবৎারপব চৎড়ারফবৎ (ঠঅঝচ) তাদের ওয়েবসাইট/অ্যাপের মাধ্যমে বাংলাদেশে কাযর্রত কোন কোন তফসিলি ব্যাংকের গ্রাহক
একাউন্ট ব্যবহার করে ঠরৎঃঁধষ পঁৎৎবহপু/ঈৎুঢ়ঃড় পঁৎৎবহপু, ঋড়ৎবরমহ পঁৎৎবহপু ইত্যাদির লেনদেন, ক্রয়-বিক্রয়, পুনঃবিক্রয়,
চ২চ বিনিময়/স্থানান্ত্মর/বাণিজ্য কাযর্ক্রম পরিচালনা করছে।
৩। এক্ষণে, ভাচুর্য়াল সম্পদ (ঠরৎঃঁধষ ধংংবঃ) ও ভাচুর্য়াল মুদ্রার (ঠরৎঃঁধষ পঁৎৎবহপু/ঈৎুঢ়ঃড় পঁৎৎবহপু) লেনদেন
এবং তাদের বিনিময়/স্থানান্ত্মর/বাণিজ্য কাযর্ক্রমের কারণে সম্ভাব্য আথির্ক ও আইনগত ঝুঁকি পরিহারের লÿ্যে নিম্নবণির্ত নিদের্শনা
প্রদান করা হলোঃ

ক) গ্রাহকের ব্যাংক একাউন্ট ব্যবহার করে ঠঅঝচ এর মাধ্যমে ঠরৎঃঁধষ পঁৎৎবহপু/ঈৎুঢ়ঃড় পঁৎৎবহপু, ঋড়ৎবরমহ
পঁৎৎবহপু ইত্যাদির লেনদেন, ক্রয়-বিক্রয়, পুনঃবিক্রয়, চ২চ বিনিময়/স্থানান্ত্মর/বাণিজ্য সংক্রান্ত্ম কাযর্ক্রম অথবা
এরূপ যেকোন ধরনের কাযের্ সহায়তা প্রদান অবিলম্বে বন্ধের পাশাপাশি এ বিষয়ে যথাযথ সতকর্তা অবলম্বনপূবর্ক
মনিটরিং কাযর্ক্রম বৃদ্ধি করতে হবে;

খ) এফই সাকুর্লার নং-২৪/২০২২ এর মাধ্যমে প্রদত্ত নিদের্শনা ব্যাংকের প্রধান কাযার্লয়, সকল শাখা, উপশাখা ও
এজেন্ট ব্যাংকিং আউটলেটসমূহের দশর্নীয় স্থানে জনসাধারণের অবগতির লক্ষ্যে তাদের বোধগম্য করে নোটিশ
বোডের্ প্রদশর্ন এবং ওয়েবসাইটের হোম পেইজ-এ প্রকাশ নিশ্চিত করাসহ সকল প্রশিক্ষণ প্রোগ্রামে
প্রশিক্ষণাথীের্দরকে সাকুর্লারটির বিষয়বস্তু অবগতকরণের নিমিত্ত প্রয়োজনীয় ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করতে হবে।
৪। ব্যাংক কোম্পানী আইন, ১৯৯১ এর ৪৫ ধারায় প্রদত্ত ÿমতাবলে এ নিদের্শনা জারি করা হলো।

আপনাদের বিশ্বস্ত্ম,

বাংলাদেশ।
বিনংরঃব: িি.িনন.ড়ৎম.নফ

ব্যাংকিং প্রবিধি ও নীতি বিভাগ

১২ অক্টোবর ২০২২
বিআরপিডি সাকুর্লার লেটার নং-৪০
তারিখ: -----------------

২৭ আশ্বিন ১৪২৯
ব্যবস্থাপনা পরিচালক/প্রধান নিবার্হী কমর্কতার্
বাংলাদেশে কাযর্রত সকল তফসিলি ব্যাংক

প্রিয় মহোদয়,
ভাচুর্য়াল সম্পদ (ঠরৎঃঁধষ ধংংবঃ) ও ভাচুর্য়াল মুদ্রা (ঠরৎঃঁধষ পঁৎৎবহপু) লেনদেন এবং তাদের
বিনিময়/স্থানান্ত্মর/বাণিজ্য (ঊীপযধহমব/ঞৎধহংভবৎ/ঞৎধফরহম) সংক্রান্ত্ম নিষেধাজ্ঞা প্রসঙ্গে।

শিরোনামোক্ত বিষয়ে ঙ্বদেশিক মুদ্রা নীতি বিভাগ কতৃর্ক ১৫ সেপ্টেম্বর ২০২২ তারিখে জারিকৃত এফই সাকুর্লার নং-২৪
এর প্রতি আপনাদের দৃষ্টি আকষর্ণ করা যাচ্ছে।
২। সূত্রোক্ত সাকুর্লারের মাধ্যমে ভাচুর্য়াল সম্পদ (ঠরৎঃঁধষ ধংংবঃ) ও ভাচুর্য়াল মুদ্রা (ঠরৎঃঁধষ পঁৎৎবহপু) লেনদেন এবং
তাদের বিনিময়/স্থানান্ত্মর/বাণিজ্যের (ঊীপযধহমব/ঞৎধহংভবৎ/ঞৎধফরহম) সাথে যুক্ত ব্যবসা ও এ সংক্রান্ত্ম যেকোন ধরনের কাযর্ক্রমে
সহায়তা প্রদান হতে বিরত থাকার জন্য নিদের্শনা দেওয়া হয়েছে। সম্প্রতি লক্ষ করা যাচ্ছে যে, বিভিন্ন বিদেশী ঠরৎঃঁধষ অংংবঃ
ঝবৎারপব চৎড়ারফবৎ (ঠঅঝচ) তাদের ওয়েবসাইট/অ্যাপের মাধ্যমে বাংলাদেশে কাযর্রত কোন কোন তফসিলি ব্যাংকের গ্রাহক
একাউন্ট ব্যবহার করে ঠরৎঃঁধষ পঁৎৎবহপু/ঈৎুঢ়ঃড় পঁৎৎবহপু, ঋড়ৎবরমহ পঁৎৎবহপু ইত্যাদির লেনদেন, ক্রয়-বিক্রয়, পুনঃবিক্রয়,
চ২চ বিনিময়/স্থানান্ত্মর/বাণিজ্য কাযর্ক্রম পরিচালনা করছে।
৩। এক্ষণে, ভাচুর্য়াল সম্পদ (ঠরৎঃঁধষ ধংংবঃ) ও ভাচুর্য়াল মুদ্রার (ঠরৎঃঁধষ পঁৎৎবহপু/ঈৎুঢ়ঃড় পঁৎৎবহপু) লেনদেন
এবং তাদের বিনিময়/স্থানান্ত্মর/বাণিজ্য কাযর্ক্রমের কারণে সম্ভাব্য আথির্ক ও আইনগত ঝুঁকি পরিহারের লÿ্যে নিম্নবণির্ত নিদের্শনা
প্রদান করা হলোঃ

ক) গ্রাহকের ব্যাংক একাউন্ট ব্যবহার করে ঠঅঝচ এর মাধ্যমে ঠরৎঃঁধষ পঁৎৎবহপু/ঈৎুঢ়ঃড় পঁৎৎবহপু, ঋড়ৎবরমহ
পঁৎৎবহপু ইত্যাদির লেনদেন, ক্রয়-বিক্রয়, পুনঃবিক্রয়, চ২চ বিনিময়/স্থানান্ত্মর/বাণিজ্য সংক্রান্ত্ম কাযর্ক্রম অথবা
এরূপ যেকোন ধরনের কাযের্ সহায়তা প্রদান অবিলম্বে বন্ধের পাশাপাশি এ বিষয়ে যথাযথ সতকর্তা অবলম্বনপূবর্ক
মনিটরিং কাযর্ক্রম বৃদ্ধি করতে হবে;

খ) এফই সাকুর্লার নং-২৪/২০২২ এর মাধ্যমে প্রদত্ত নিদের্শনা ব্যাংকের প্রধান কাযার্লয়, সকল শাখা, উপশাখা ও
এজেন্ট ব্যাংকিং আউটলেটসমূহের দশর্নীয় স্থানে জনসাধারণের অবগতির লক্ষ্যে তাদের বোধগম্য করে নোটিশ
বোডের্ প্রদশর্ন এবং ওয়েবসাইটের হোম পেইজ-এ প্রকাশ নিশ্চিত করাসহ সকল প্রশিক্ষণ প্রোগ্রামে
প্রশিক্ষণাথীের্দরকে সাকুর্লারটির বিষয়বস্তু অবগতকরণের নিমিত্ত প্রয়োজনীয় ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করতে হবে।
৪। ব্যাংক কোম্পানী আইন, ১৯৯১ এর ৪৫ ধারায় প্রদত্ত ÿমতাবলে এ নিদের্শনা জারি করা হলো।

আথির্ক প্রতিষ্ঠান ও বাজার বিভাগ
বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংক
প্রধান কাযার্লয়
ঢাকা।
ডবনংরঃব: িি.িনন.ড়ৎম.নফ

ডিএফআইএম সাকুর্লার লেটার নং-২৪
ব্যবস্থাপনা পরিচালক/প্রধান নিবার্হী কমর্কতার্
বাংলাদেশে কাযর্রত সকল আথির্ক প্রতিষ্ঠান।

প্রিয় মহোদয়,
ভাচুর্য়াল সম্পদ (ঠরৎঃঁধষ ধংংবঃ) ও ভাচুর্য়াল মুদ্রা (ঠরৎঃঁধষ ঈঁৎৎবহপু) লেনদেন
এবং তাদের বিনিময়/স্থানান্ত্মর/বাণিজ্য (ঊীপযধহমব/ঞৎধহংভবৎ/ঞৎধফরহম) সংক্রান্ত্ম নিষেধাজ্ঞা প্রসঙ্গে।
শিরোনামোক্ত বিষয়ে বৈদেশিক মুদ্রা নীতি বিভাগ কতৃর্ক ১৫ সেপ্টেম্বর ২০২২ তারিখে জারিকৃত এফই সাকুর্লার নং-
২৪ এর প্রতি আপনাদের দৃষ্টি আকষর্ণ করা যাচ্ছে।
২। সম্প্রতি লক্ষ্য করা যাচ্ছে যে, বিভিন্ন বিদেশী ঠরৎঃঁধষ অংংবঃ ঝবৎারপব চৎড়ারফবৎ (ঠঅঝচ) তাদের
ওয়েবসাইট/অ্যাপের মাধ্যমে বাংলাদেশে কাযর্রত কোন কোন তফসিলি ব্যাংকের গ্রাহক একাউন্ট ও গঋঝ একাউন্ট ব্যবহার
করে ঠরৎঃঁধষ পঁৎৎবহপু/ঈৎুঢ়ঃড় পঁৎৎবহপু, ঋড়ৎবরমহ পঁৎৎবহপু ইত্যাদির লেনদেন, ক্রয়-বিক্রয়, পুনঃবিক্রয়, চ২চ
বিনিময়/স্থানান্ত্মর/বাণিজ্য কাযর্ক্রম পরিচালনা করছে। ভাচুর্য়াল সম্পদ (ঠরৎঃঁধষ অংংবঃ) ও ভাচুর্য়াল মুদ্রা (ঠরৎঃঁধষ
ঈঁৎৎবহপু) লেনদেন এবং তাদের বিনিময়/স্থানান্ত্মর/বাণিজ্যের (ঊীপযধহমব/ঞৎধহংভবৎ/ঞৎধফরহম) সাথে যুক্ত ব্যবসা ও
এ সংক্রান্ত্ম যে কোন ধরনের কাযর্ক্রমে সহায়তা প্রদান হতে বিরত থাকার জন্য সূত্রোক্ত সাকুর্লারের মাধ্যমে বাংলাদেশে কাযর্রত
সকল তফসিলি ব্যাংক, আথির্ক প্রতিষ্ঠান এবং বৈদেশিক মুদ্রা লেনদেনের সাথে সম্পৃক্ত স্টেকহোল্ডারদেরকে নিদের্শনা প্রদান
করা হয়েছে।
৩। এমতাবস্থায়, বৈদেশিক মুদ্রা নীতি বিভাগ কতৃর্ক জারিকৃত এফই সাকুর্লার নং-২৪, তারিখঃ ১৫/০৯/২০২২-এ
প্রদত্ত নিদের্শনা আপনাদের প্রতিষ্ঠানের প্রধান কাযার্লয় এবং শাখাসমূহের দশর্নীয় স্থানে জনসাধারণের বোধগম্য করে প্রদশর্ন,
প্রতিষ্ঠানের ওয়েবসাইটে প্রকাশ নিশ্চিত করাসহ আপনাদের যে কোন ট্রেনিং প্রোগ্রামে প্রশিÿণাথীের্দরকে সাকুর্লারটির বিষয়বস্তু
অবহিতকরণের প্রয়োজনীয় ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণের জন্য আপনাদেরকে নিদের্শনা প্রদান করা হলো।
৪। আথির্ক প্রতিষ্ঠান আইন, ১৯৯৩ এর ১৮(ছ) ধারায় প্রদত্ত ÿমতাবলে জনস্বাথের্ এ আদেশ জারি করা হলো।

আথির্ক প্রতিষ্ঠান ও বাজার বিভাগ
বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংক
প্রধান কাযার্লয়
ঢাকা।
ডবনংরঃব: িি.িনন.ড়ৎম.নফ

ডিএফআইএম সাকুর্লার লেটার নং-২৪
ব্যবস্থাপনা পরিচালক/প্রধান নিবার্হী কমর্কতার্
বাংলাদেশে কাযর্রত সকল আথির্ক প্রতিষ্ঠান।

প্রিয় মহোদয়,
ভাচুর্য়াল সম্পদ (ঠরৎঃঁধষ ধংংবঃ) ও ভাচুর্য়াল মুদ্রা (ঠরৎঃঁধষ ঈঁৎৎবহপু) লেনদেন
এবং তাদের বিনিময়/স্থানান্ত্মর/বাণিজ্য (ঊীপযধহমব/ঞৎধহংভবৎ/ঞৎধফরহম) সংক্রান্ত্ম নিষেধাজ্ঞা প্রসঙ্গে।
শিরোনামোক্ত বিষয়ে বৈদেশিক মুদ্রা নীতি বিভাগ কতৃর্ক ১৫ সেপ্টেম্বর ২০২২ তারিখে জারিকৃত এফই সাকুর্লার নং-
২৪ এর প্রতি আপনাদের দৃষ্টি আকষর্ণ করা যাচ্ছে।
২। সম্প্রতি লক্ষ্য করা যাচ্ছে যে, বিভিন্ন বিদেশী ঠরৎঃঁধষ অংংবঃ ঝবৎারপব চৎড়ারফবৎ (ঠঅঝচ) তাদের
ওয়েবসাইট/অ্যাপের মাধ্যমে বাংলাদেশে কাযর্রত কোন কোন তফসিলি ব্যাংকের গ্রাহক একাউন্ট ও গঋঝ একাউন্ট ব্যবহার
করে ঠরৎঃঁধষ পঁৎৎবহপু/ঈৎুঢ়ঃড় পঁৎৎবহপু, ঋড়ৎবরমহ পঁৎৎবহপু ইত্যাদির লেনদেন, ক্রয়-বিক্রয়, পুনঃবিক্রয়, চ২চ
বিনিময়/স্থানান্ত্মর/বাণিজ্য কাযর্ক্রম পরিচালনা করছে। ভাচুর্য়াল সম্পদ (ঠরৎঃঁধষ অংংবঃ) ও ভাচুর্য়াল মুদ্রা (ঠরৎঃঁধষ
ঈঁৎৎবহপু) লেনদেন এবং তাদের বিনিময়/স্থানান্ত্মর/বাণিজ্যের (ঊীপযধহমব/ঞৎধহংভবৎ/ঞৎধফরহম) সাথে যুক্ত ব্যবসা ও
এ সংক্রান্ত্ম যে কোন ধরনের কাযর্ক্রমে সহায়তা প্রদান হতে বিরত থাকার জন্য সূত্রোক্ত সাকুর্লারের মাধ্যমে বাংলাদেশে কাযর্রত
সকল তফসিলি ব্যাংক, আথির্ক প্রতিষ্ঠান এবং বৈদেশিক মুদ্রা লেনদেনের সাথে সম্পৃক্ত স্টেকহোল্ডারদেরকে নিদের্শনা প্রদান
করা হয়েছে।
৩। এমতাবস্থায়, বৈদেশিক মুদ্রা নীতি বিভাগ কতৃর্ক জারিকৃত এফই সাকুর্লার নং-২৪, তারিখঃ ১৫/০৯/২০২২-এ
প্রদত্ত নিদের্শনা আপনাদের প্রতিষ্ঠানের প্রধান কাযার্লয় এবং শাখাসমূহের দশর্নীয় স্থানে জনসাধারণের বোধগম্য করে প্রদশর্ন,
প্রতিষ্ঠানের ওয়েবসাইটে প্রকাশ নিশ্চিত করাসহ আপনাদের যে কোন ট্রেনিং প্রোগ্রামে প্রশিÿণাথীের্দরকে সাকুর্লারটির বিষয়বস্তু
অবহিতকরণের প্রয়োজনীয় ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণের জন্য আপনাদেরকে নিদের্শনা প্রদান করা হলো।
৪। আথির্ক প্রতিষ্ঠান আইন, ১৯৯৩ এর ১৮(ছ) ধারায় প্রদত্ত ÿমতাবলে জনস্বাথের্ এ আদেশ জারি করা হলো।

document_analyses.executive_summary: Bangladesh Bank granted permission for Palli Sanchoy Bank to undergo a 5-day downtime (approximately 120 hours) for the Go-Live of its new Digital Banking Solution (DBS).
document_analyses.purpose: To grant formal approval for a scheduled downtime of 5 days for Palli Sanchoy Bank to ensure secure migration and Go-Live of its Digital Banking Solutions under statutory powers.
document_analyses.background: Palli Sanchoy Bank is implementing a new Digital Banking Solution (DBS) requiring a migration and Go-Live process.
key_changes: Scheduled complete suspension of all banking operations and services of Palli Sanchoy Bank for 5 days (approx. 120 hours).

impact_summary.banking_operations: All banking operations and services of Palli Sanchoy Bank will remain completely suspended for 5 days.
impact_summary.compliance: Mandatory adherence to the approved downtime window and statutory provisions.
impact_summary.risk_management: Ensures data accuracy and consistency post-migration during the Go-Live process.
impact_summary.technology: Transition to the new Digital Banking Solution (DBS).

classification.subject: পল্লী সঞ্চয় ব্যাংকের Digital Banking Solutions (DBS) এর Go live এর নিমিত্ত ডাউনটাইমের অনুমোদন প্রসঙ্গে।
classification.regulatory_topic: Digital Banking Solutions Go-Live Downtime Approval

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank granted permission for Palli Sanchoy Bank to undergo a 5-day downtime (approximately 120 hours) for the Go-Live of its new Digital Banking Solution (DBS).
executive_summary.detailed_summary: Under the powers conferred by section 45 of the Bank Company Act, 1991, Bangladesh Bank has approved a scheduled downtime for Palli Sanchoy Bank. All banking operations and services of the bank will remain completely suspended from November 1, 2026 (Sunday) at 12:01 AM to November 5, 2026 (Thursday) at 11:59 PM to ensure safe, orderly, and accurate execution of the new Digital Banking Solution (DBS) Go-Live and to ensure data integrity and consistency post-migration, accompanied by adequate publicity.
executive_summary.background: Palli Sanchoy Bank is implementing a new Digital Banking Solution (DBS) requiring a migration and Go-Live process.
executive_summary.purpose: To grant formal approval for a scheduled downtime of 5 days for Palli Sanchoy Bank to ensure secure migration and Go-Live of its Digital Banking Solutions under statutory powers.
key_changes: Scheduled complete suspension of all banking operations and services of Palli Sanchoy Bank for 5 days (approx. 120 hours).

provisions.heading: ডাউনটাইমের সময়সূচি
provisions.verbatim_text: পল্লী সঞ্চয় ব্যাংকের নতুন Digital Banking Solution (DBS)-এর Go-Live কার্যক্রম নিরাপদ, সুষ্ঠু ও নিখুঁতভাবে সম্পন্ন করা এবং মাইগ্রেশন-পরবর্তী তথ্যের যথার্থতা ও সামঞ্জস্য নিশ্চিত করার নিমিত্ত প্রয়োজনীয় ও পর্যাপ্ত প্রচারণার অব্যাহত রাখার শর্তে নিম্নবর্ণিত সময়সূচী অনুযায়ী ব্যাংকটিকে ডাউনটাইমের অনুমতি প্রদান করা হইয়াছেঃ কার্যক্রম: নির্ধারিত ডাউনটাইম শুরু | তারিখ: ০১ নভেম্বর ২০২৬ (রবিবার) | সময়: রাত ১২:০১ টা | ডাউনটাইম ব্যাপ্তি: ৫ দিন (প্রায় ১২০ ঘন্টা) | পরিসেবাসমূহ: সকল সেবা। কার্যক্রম: নির্ধারিত ডাউনটাইম শেষ | তারিখ: ০৫ নভেম্বর ২০২৬ (বৃহস্পতিবার) | সময়: রাত ১১:৫৯ টা। উক্ত সময়ে ব্যাংকটির সকল ধরনের ব্যাংকিং কার্যক্রম ও সেবা সম্পূর্ণভাবে বন্ধ থাকিবে।
provisions.normalized_explanation: Palli Sanchoy Bank is granted permission for a 5-day downtime from November 1, 2026, 12:01 AM to November 5, 2026, 11:59 PM to implement its Digital Banking Solution (DBS) Go-Live under the condition that adequate publicity is maintained.

provisions.heading: আইনি ক্ষমতা
provisions.verbatim_text: ব্যাংক কোম্পানী আইন, ১৯৯১-এর ৪৫ ধারায় প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতা বলে বর্ণিত অনুমোদন প্রদান করা হইয়াছে।
provisions.normalized_explanation: This approval is granted under the authority provided by Section 45 of the Bank Company Act, 1991.

obligations.title: Publicity and Maintenance of Downtime Execution
obligations.requirement_description: Ensure necessary and adequate publicity regarding the downtime and execute the DBS Go-Live safely and accurately within the specified schedule.
obligations.verbatim_quote: পল্লী সঞ্চয় ব্যাংকের নতুন Digital Banking Solution (DBS)-এর Go-Live কার্যক্রম নিরাপদ, সুষ্ঠু ও নিখুঁতভাবে সম্পন্ন করা এবং মাইগ্রেশন-পরবর্তী তথ্যের যথার্থতা ও সামঞ্জস্য নিশ্চিত করার নিমিত্ত প্রয়োজনীয় ও পর্যাপ্ত প্রচ প্রচারণা অব্যাহত রাখার শর্তে নিম্নবর্ণিত সময়সূচী অনুযায়ী ব্যাংকটিকে ডাউনটাইমের অনুমতি প্রদান করা হইয়াছেঃ
obligations.applicability_conditions: Execution of DBS Go-Live
obligations.required_evidence: Adequate publicity and successful system migration

document_analyses.executive_summary: Bangladesh Bank issued guidelines requiring scheduled commercial banks and financial institutions to identify and report Ultimate Beneficial Owners holding 10 percent or more equity or control in borrowing entities.
document_analyses.purpose: To establish rigorous identification and reporting standards for Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs) in borrowing entities exceeding specific credit thresholds.
document_analyses.background: Issued under Section 45 of the Bank Company Act, 1991 to combat trade-based money laundering, illicit financial flows, and willful default through shell corporations.
key_changes: Establishment of a 10 percent threshold for Ultimate Beneficial Ownership identification.
Mandatory collection of verified UBO declarations and NID/Passport copies for credit lines exceeding BDT 5 Crore prior to disbursement or renewal.
Requirement for biannual UBO compliance status reporting to BRPD and BFIU within 15 days of each half-year end.
Supersession of BRPD Circular Letter No. 05 dated 12 March 2018.

impact_summary.banking_operations: Requires banks to update credit processing workflows to collect and verify UBO information for all credit lines exceeding BDT 5 Crore.
impact_summary.credit: Adds a mandatory prerequisite of UBO verification prior to disbursing or renewing credit lines above BDT 5 Crore.
impact_summary.compliance: Institutes a new biannual reporting requirement to BRPD and BFIU for monitoring UBO compliance status.
impact_summary.risk_management: Strengthens AML/CFT measures and mitigates risks related to trade-based money laundering, illicit financial flows, and shell corporations.

classification.subject: Guidelines on Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Disclosure

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank issued guidelines requiring scheduled commercial banks and financial institutions to identify and report Ultimate Beneficial Owners holding 10 percent or more equity or control in borrowing entities.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: To combat trade-based money laundering, illicit financial flows, and willful default through shell corporations, Bangladesh Bank has introduced comprehensive guidelines on Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) disclosure under Section 45 of the Bank Company Act, 1991. The circular mandates that banks and financial institutions identify natural persons holding 10 percent or more equity interest, voting rights, or controlling management authority. Verified UBO declarations and National ID or Passport copies must be obtained prior to loan disbursement or credit line renewal exceeding BDT 5 Crore. Furthermore, banks are required to submit biannual compliance status reports to BRPD and BFIU within 15 days of each half-year end. This circular supersedes BRPD Circular Letter No. 05 dated 12 March 2018.

provisions.heading: Threshold for Ultimate Beneficial Ownership
provisions.verbatim_text: Any natural person holding directly or indirectly 10 percent or more equity interest, voting rights, or controlling management authority in a borrowing entity must be identified as an Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO).
provisions.normalized_explanation: Defines an Ultimate Beneficial Owner as any natural person holding at least 10% of equity, voting rights, or control in a borrower directly or indirectly.

provisions.heading: Mandatory Obligations
provisions.verbatim_text:
All scheduled commercial banks must obtain verified UBO declarations and National ID / Passport copies prior to loan disbursement or renewal of credit lines exceeding BDT 5 Crore.
Banks must submit biannual UBO compliance status reports to BRPD and BFIU within 15 days of each half-year end.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates banks to collect UBO declarations and identification documents for loans over BDT 5 Crore and to submit biannual compliance reports.

executive_summary.detailed_summary: This circular letter amends the previously issued circulars concerning the 20,000 crore Taka facilitation scheme for closed industries and service sectors. The scheme's name is officially changed from a 'Pre-finance Scheme' to a 'Refinance Scheme'. Key amendments include requirements for borrowers to provide a declaration confirming no history of money laundering, fraud, fund diversion, or loan misuse. Furthermore, transactions under the scheme must be routed through Escrow or Revenue accounts, aligning with prior guidelines. Additionally, procedures for submitting refinance applications through bank boards or executive committees have been updated with strict post-disbursement timelines and provisions for extended delays.

provisions.heading: স্কিমের নাম পরিবর্তন এবং নির্দেশনাসমূহ
provisions.verbatim_text: সূত্রোক্ত সাকুর্লার/সাকুর্লার লেটারসমূহের মাধ্যমে "বন্ধ শিল্প ও সেবা খাত সহায়ক প্রাক-অথার্য়ন স্কিম" (Closed Industry and Service Sector Facilitation Pre-finance Scheme) শিরোনামীয় ২০,০০০ (বিশ হাজার) কোটি টাকার একটি স্কিম গঠনকরত এ সংক্রান্ত্ম অনুসরণীয় নীতিমালা জারি করা হয়। এক্ষণে, উক্ত স্কিমের কাযর্ক্রমে গতিশীলতা আনয়নের লÿ্যে নিম্নোক্ত নিদের্শনাসমূহ অনুসরণীয় হবে:
provisions.normalized_explanation: To bring dynamism to the operations of the 20,000 crore Taka scheme, specific instructions and amendments replace previous clauses.

provisions.heading: স্কিমের নাম
provisions.verbatim_text: "২। স্কিমের নাম: এ স্কিমের নাম হবে "বন্ধ শিল্প ও সেবা খাত সহায়ক পুনঃঅথার্য়ন স্কিম" (Closed Industry and Service Sector Facilitation Re-finance Scheme)। "
provisions.normalized_explanation: The scheme is officially renamed from 'Pre-finance Scheme' to 'Re-finance Scheme'.

provisions.heading: গ্রাহক পযাের্য় ঋণ প্রাপ্তির যোগ্যতা
provisions.verbatim_text: "৮। গ্রাহক পযাের্য় ঋণ প্রাপ্তির যোগ্যতা: জ) আলোচ্য স্কিমের আওতায় ঋণ প্রত্যাশী গ্রাহক ইতোপূবের্ অথর্পাচার, জাল-জালিয়াতি, ফান্ড ডাইভাশর্ন অথবা ঋণের অথর্ অপব্যবহার করেনি মমের্ ব্যাংক কতৃর্ক গ্রাহক হতে একটি ঘোষণাপত্র গ্রহণ করতে হবে।"
provisions.normalized_explanation: Banks must collect a declaration from loan applicants confirming they have not previously engaged in money laundering, forgery, fund diversion, or misuse of loan funds.

provisions.heading: ঋণের ব্যবহার
provisions.verbatim_text: "৯। ঋণের ব্যবহার: ঘ) ঋণগ্রহীতা যে ব্যাংক হতে প্রকল্প ঋণ গ্রহণ করছেন সে ব্যাংক হতে এ স্কিমের আওতায় ঋণ গ্রহণের ক্ষেত্রে অগ্রাধিকার প্রাপ্ত হবেন। এ স্কিমের আওতায় প্রদত্ত ঋণ/বিনিয়োগের লেনদেন গ্রাহকের Escrow account অথবা Revenue account (যে নামেই অভিহিত হোক না কেন) এর মাধ্যমে সম্পাদন করতে হবে। এক্ষেত্রে প্রকল্প ঋণ প্রদানের ক্ষেত্রে সংশিস্নষ্ট ব্যাংকে প্রকল্পের আয় হিসাব খোলার বাধ্যবাধকতা প্রসঙ্গে জারিকৃত বিআরপিডি সাকুর্লার নং-০১, তারিখ: ১৮ জানুয়ারি ২০২৪ এর নিদের্শনা যথাযথভাবে অনুসরণ করতে হবে;"
provisions.normalized_explanation: Borrowers are prioritized for scheme loans from their project-lending bank. All transactions under this scheme must occur through an Escrow or Revenue account, following BRPD Circular No-01 of 2024 regarding project income accounts.

provisions.heading: পুনঃঅথার্য়নের জন্য আবেদন পদ্ধতি
provisions.verbatim_text: "১৩। পুনঃঅথার্য়নের জন্য আবেদন পদ্ধতি: ক) সংশিস্নষ্ট ব্যাংক পরিচালনা পষের্দর অথবা পষর্দ কতৃর্ক অপির্ত ক্ষমতাবলে পষর্দ নিবার্হী কমিটির (Board Executive Committee) অনুমোদনক্রমে ঋণ মঞ্জুরকরত ঋণ বিতরণের পরবতীর্ সপ্তাহের মধ্যে প্রয়োজনীয় তথ্য ও কাগজপত্রাদিসহ নিধাির্রত ছকে (সংযোজনী-ক) পরিচালক, ব্যাংকিং প্রবিধি ও নীতি বিভাগ-৩, বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংক, প্রধান কাযার্লয় বরাবর পুনঃঅথার্য়নের জন্য আবেদন করতে হবে। তবে কোনো কারণে পরবতীর্ সপ্তাহের মধ্যে পুনঃঅথার্য়নের আবেদন দাখিলে ব্যথর্ হলে উপযুক্ত কারণ উলেস্নখপূবর্ক তৎপরবতীর্ আরও ১৫(পনেরো) দিনের মধ্যে আবেদন দাখিল করা যাবে; "
provisions.normalized_explanation: Banks must apply for refinance within the week following loan disbursement (approved by the board or executive committee). If delayed, applications can be submitted within an additional 15 days with valid reasons.

provisions.heading: আইনি ক্ষমতা ও কার্যকারিতা
provisions.verbatim_text: ৩। ব্যাংক কোম্পানী আইন, ১৯৯১ এর ৪৫ ধারায় প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে এ নিদের্শনা জারি করা হল, যা অবিলম্বে কাযর্কর হবে।
provisions.normalized_explanation: This directive is issued under Section 45 of the Bank Company Act, 1991, and takes effect immediately.

obligations.title: Obtain Borrower Declaration on Financial Integrity
obligations.requirement_description: Banks must obtain a written declaration from the loan applicant stating they have no prior history of money laundering, forgery, fund diversion, or misuse of loan funds.
obligations.verbatim_quote: আলোচ্য স্কিমের আওতায় ঋণ প্রত্যাশী গ্রাহক ইতোপূবের্ অথর্পাচার, জাল-জালিয়াতি, ফান্ড ডাইভাশর্ন অথবা ঋণের অথর্ অপব্যবহার করেনি মমের্ ব্যাংক কতৃর্ক গ্রাহক হতে একটি ঘোষণাপত্র গ্রহণ করতে হবে।

obligations.required_evidence: Signed customer declaration document

obligations.title: Route Scheme Transactions via Escrow or Revenue Account
obligations.requirement_description: All loan and investment transactions under the scheme must be executed through the customer's Escrow or Revenue account, complying with BRPD Circular No-01 dated January 18, 2024.

obligations.applicability_conditions: During the disbursement and utilization of loans under the scheme.
obligations.required_evidence: Escrow or Revenue account transaction statements

obligations.title: Submit Refinance Application Post-Disbursement
obligations.requirement_description: Following board or executive committee approval and loan disbursement, banks must apply for refinance to Bangladesh Bank within the following week. If missed, application can be made within a further 15 days with proper justification.
obligations.verbatim_quote: ঋণ বিতরণের পরবতীর্ সপ্তাহের মধ্যে প্রয়োজনীয় তথ্য ও কাগজপত্রাদিসহ নিধাির্রত ছকে (সংযোজনী-ক) পরিচালক, ব্যাংকিং প্রবিধি ও নীতি বিভাগ-৩, বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংক, প্রধান কাযার্লয় বরাবর পুনঃঅথার্য়নের জন্য আবেদন করতে হবে। তবে কোনো কারণে পরবতীর্ সপ্তাহের মধ্যে পুনঃঅথার্য়নের আবেদন দাখিলে ব্যথর্ হলে উপযুক্ত কারণ উলেস্নখপূবর্ক তৎপরবতীর্ আরও ১৫(পনেরো) দিনের মধ্যে আবেদন দাখিল করা যাবে;

applicability.conditional_rules: Applies to all scheduled banks operating in Bangladesh participating in the Closed Industry and Service Sector Refinance Scheme.

deadlines.trigger_event: Loan disbursement under the scheme triggers the 1-week (or subsequent 15-day grace period) refinance application deadline.

document_analyses.executive_summary: Summary for gate test.

Bangladesh Bank announced a general holiday on October 29, 2026, for all scheduled banks and their branches/sub-branches within the Thakurgaon-1 parliamentary constituency due to the upcoming by-election.
document_analyses.purpose: To facilitate voting in the by-election of the Thakurgaon-1 parliamentary constituency by granting a general holiday to banking institutions located in the area.
document_analyses.background: Ministry of Public Administration memorandum number 05.00.0000.000.175.08.0020.24-98 dated October 15, 2026.
key_changes: Closure of all scheduled bank regional offices, branches, and sub-branches within the Thakurgaon-1 constituency on October 29, 2026.

impact_summary.banking_operations: Temporary suspension of physical banking operations and branch services within the Thakurgaon-1 constituency on October 29, 2026.
impact_summary.credit: Loan processing, disbursements, and collections through branches in the specified area will be paused for the day.
impact_summary.compliance: Mandatory adherence to the general holiday closure notice issued under Section 45 of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
impact_summary.risk_management: Branch security and cash management measures aligned with holiday closures.
impact_summary.technology: Digital banking channels remain operational, though physical branch services are suspended.

document_analyses.executive_summary: Bangladesh Bank issued an exemption under Section 121 of the Bank Company Act, 1991, allowing a consortium led by City Bank PLC to provide a BDT 3,000 crore syndicated working capital loan facility to five defaulter concerns of City Group until December 31, 2027, subject to specific conditions.

document_analyses.background: The notification is issued using powers conferred under Section 121 of the Bank Company Act, 1991 (Act No. 14 of 1991), providing an exemption from Section 27KaKa(3) for classified/defaulting entities belonging to City Group.
key_changes: Exemption from Section 27KaKa(3) of the Bank Company Act, 1991 until December 31, 2027.

impact_summary.banking_operations: Enables City Bank PLC and participating syndicate banks to structure and disburse a large working capital credit facility to defaulting entities under regulatory relaxation.
impact_summary.credit: Provides BDT 3,000 crore in syndicated working capital credit to five loan-defaulting entities under City Group.

classification.department: ব্যাংকিং প্রবিধি ও নীতি বিভাগ-২ (Banking Regulation and Policy Department-2)
classification.subject: সিটি গ্রম্নপভুক্ত পাঁচটি প্রতিষ্ঠানের অনুকূলে সিন্ডিকেটেড চলতি মূলধন ঋণ সুবিধা প্রদানে ব্যাংক-কোম্পানী আইন, ১৯৯১ এর ২৭কক(৩) ধারা থেকে অব্যাহতি প্রদান প্রসঙ্গে।

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank issued an exemption under Section 121 of the Bank Company Act, 1991, allowing a consortium led by City Bank PLC to provide a BDT 3,000 crore syndicated working capital loan facility to five defaulter concerns of City Group until December 31, 2027, subject to specific conditions.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: Through Circular Letter No. 18 and Notification No-BRPD-2(R-1)(Law Review)717/2026-4454 dated November 04, 2026, Bangladesh Bank invoked its powers under Section 121 of the Bank Company Act, 1991 to exempt the provisions of Section 27KaKa(3) of the same Act. This exemption permits City Bank PLC and its syndicate to extend a syndicated working capital loan of BDT 3,000 crore to five defaulting entities under City Group (City Seed Crashing Industries Ltd., City Sugar Industries Ltd., City Edible Oil Ltd., City Dal Mills Ltd., and Shampa Flour Mills Ltd.) up to December 31, 2027. The exemption is subject to strict conditions including no creation of government or Bangladesh Bank liability, provision of unencumbered registered mortgages as reasonable collateral, routing proceeds of goods sold through a specific bank account for priority proportional repayment of syndicate dues, and purchase/processing of raw materials as security agent representatives and custodians.
executive_summary.background: The notification is issued using powers conferred under Section 121 of the Bank Company Act, 1991 (Act No. 14 of 1991), providing an exemption from Section 27KaKa(3) for classified/defaulting entities belonging to City Group.
executive_summary.purpose: To facilitate syndicated working capital financing amounting to BDT 3,000 crore for five specific City Group concerns through a consortium led by City Bank PLC under specified safeguards.
key_changes: Exemption from Section 27KaKa(3) of the Bank Company Act, 1991 until December 31, 2027.
Permission to extend BDT 3,000 crore syndicated working capital facility to five defaulting entities of City Group.

provisions.heading: অব্যাহতি প্রদান
provisions.verbatim_text: ব্যাংক-কোম্পানী আইন, ১৯৯১ (১৯৯১ সনের ১৪ নং আইন) এর ১২১ ধারায় প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতা বলে এতদ্বারা সকলের অবগতির জন্য জানানো যাচ্ছে যে, সিটি গ্রুপভুক্ত খণখেলাপি পাঁচটি প্রতিষ্ঠান- সিটি সিড ক্রাশিং ইন্ডস্ট্রিজ লিঃ, সিটি সুগার ইন্ডাস্ট্রিজ লিঃ, সিটি এডিবল অয়েল লিঃ, সিটি ডাল মিলস লিঃ ও শম্পা ফ্লাওয়ার মিলস্‌ লিঃ এর অনুকূলে ৩০০০ (তিন হাজার) কোটি টাকার চলতি মূলধন (ওয়ার্কিং ক্যাপিটাল) সুবিধা প্রদানের ক্ষেত্রে সিটি ব্যাংক পিএলসি-এর নেতৃত্বে গঠিতব্য সিন্ডিকেটেড অর্থায়নের জন্য ব্যাংক কোম্পানী আইন ১৯৯১ এর ২৭কক(৩) ধারায় বর্ণিত বিধান আগামী ৩১ ডিসেম্বর ২০২৭ পর্যন্ত কার্যকর হবে নাঃ
provisions.normalized_explanation: Invoking Section 121 of the Bank Company Act, 1991, the restrictions under Section 27KaKa(3) shall not apply until December 31, 2027, for providing a BDT 3,000 crore syndicated working capital loan led by City Bank PLC to five loan-defaulting entities of City Group.

provisions.verbatim_text: (ক) প্রস্তাবিত খণ-সুবিধার বিপরীতে সরকার ও বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংকের কোনো দায় সৃষ্টি হবে না এবং ভবিষ্যতে সিটি ব্যাংক পিএলসি বা সিন্ডিকেটভুক্ত অন্য কোন ব্যাংক বা আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান সরকার ও বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংকের কাছ থেকে কোনোরূপ আর্থিক সহায়তা দাবি করতে পারবে না;
provisions.normalized_explanation: No liability shall be created for the government or Bangladesh Bank against the proposed credit facility, and participating banks/financial institutions cannot claim any financial assistance from them.

provisions.verbatim_text: (খ) প্রস্তাবিত খণ সুবিধার বিপরীতে যুক্তিসংগত জামানত নিশ্চিত করতে সিটি গ্ুপ তাদের অন্য কোনো খণ বা দায়ে আবদ্ধ নয় (un-encumbered) এমন সম্পত্তি রেজিস্টার্ড মর্টগেজ হিসেবে প্রদান করবে;
provisions.normalized_explanation: City Group must provide un-encumbered properties as registered mortgages to ensure reasonable collateral against the proposed credit facility.

provisions.verbatim_text: (গ) সিন্ডিকেটেড খণের টাকায় কেনা পণ্য বিক্রয় করে যে টাকা পাওয়া যাবে, তা একটি নির্দিষ্ট ব্যাংক হিসাবে জমা রাখতে হবে এবং সেখান থেকে আনুপাতিক হারে সিন্ডিকেটেড খণ সুবিধা প্রদানকারী ব্যাংকসমূহের পাওনা অগ্রাধিকারভিত্তিতে নিয়মিত পরিশোধ করতে হবে;
provisions.normalized_explanation: Proceeds from the sale of goods purchased via syndicated loan funds must be deposited into a specific bank account, from which syndicate lenders' dues must be regularly serviced on a priority and proportional basis.

provisions.verbatim_text: (ঘ) সিন্ডিকেটেড খণের টাকায় আমদানিকৃত কীচামাল খণগ্রহীতা প্রতিষ্ঠানসমূহ খণদাতা ব্যাংকসমূহের সিকিউরিটি এজেন্টের প্রতিনিধি হিসেবে ক্রয় করবে এবং জিন্মাদার হিসেবে তা প্রক্রিয়াজাত করবে।
provisions.normalized_explanation: Raw materials imported using the syndicated loan must be purchased by borrowing entities as representatives of the lender banks' security agent and processed as custodians/bailees.

obligations.title: Collateral Provision via Unencumbered Property
obligations.requirement_description: City Group must provide unencumbered property as a registered mortgage to secure the proposed credit facility.
obligations.verbatim_quote: প্রস্তাবিত খণ সুবিধার বিপরীতে যুক্তিসংগত জামানত নিশ্চিত করতে সিটি গ্ুপ তাদের অন্য কোনো খণ বা দায়ে আবদ্ধ নয় (un-encumbered) এমন সম্পত্তি রেজিস্টার্ড মর্টগেজ হিসেবে প্রদান করবে;

obligations.verbatim_quote: সিন্ডিকেটেড খণের টাকায় কেনা পণ্য বিক্রয় করে যে টাকা পাওয়া যাবে, তা একটি নির্দিষ্ট ব্যাংক হিসাবে জমা রাখতে হবে এবং সেখান থেকে আনুপাতিক হারে সিন্ডিকেটেড খণ সুবিধা প্রদানকারী ব্যাংকসমূহের পাওনা অগ্রাধিকারভিত্তিতে নিয়মিত পরিশোধ করতে হবে;

obligations.verbatim_quote: সিন্ডিকেটেড খণের টাকায় আমদানিকৃত কীচামাল খণগ্রহীতা প্রতিষ্ঠানসমূহ খণদাতা ব্যাংকসমূহের সিকিউরিটি এজেন্টের প্রতিনিধি হিসেবে ক্রয় করবে এবং জিন্মাদার হিসেবে তা প্রক্রিয়াজাত করবে।

classification.subject: Master Policy on Loan Classification and Provisioning Alignment with IFRS 9

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank introduces a master policy aligning loan classification and general provisioning standards with IFRS 9.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: The circular establishes a mandatory three-stage credit facility classification framework for all scheduled commercial banks. Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.
executive_summary.background: Issued under powers conferred by the Bank Company Act, 1991 to strengthen risk management in the banking sector.
executive_summary.purpose: Harmonization of credit risk measurement with international accounting standard IFRS 9.
key_changes: Introduction of mandatory 3-stage credit classification framework
Mandatory general provision of 5.00% on Stage 2 underperforming loans
Ban on interest reversal into income without prior written approval from Bangladesh Bank

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk since initial recognition. General provision of 1.00% must be maintained.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: Stage 2 (Underperforming): Loans exhibiting significant increase in credit risk (SICR) or overdue past 30 days up to 89 days. General provision of 5.00% must be maintained.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: The amended provisions set forth in this Circular shall come into force with effect from 01 January 2025. All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.title: Maintain 5.00% General Provision on Stage 2 Loans
obligations.requirement_description: Scheduled commercial banks must maintain 5.00% general provisioning on credit facilities categorized under Stage 2 (overdue 30-89 days).
obligations.verbatim_quote: Stage 2 (Underperforming): Loans exhibiting significant increase in credit risk (SICR) or overdue past 30 days up to 89 days. General provision of 5.00% must be maintained.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.title: Submit Initial IFRS 9 Readiness Report
obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.
obligations.verbatim_quote: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All scheduled commercial banks
obligations.required_evidence: Board-approved IFRS 9 transition readiness report
obligations.consequence: Supervisory warning and inspection scrutiny

exemptions: Islamic Banks are covered under separate shariah-compliant guidelines
applicability.conditional_rules: Applies to all loan portfolios exceeding initial recognition

deadlines.trigger_event: Circular publication on Bangladesh Bank website

classification.subject: Master Policy on Loan Classification and Provisioning Alignment with IFRS 9

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank introduces a master policy aligning loan classification and general provisioning standards with IFRS 9.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: The circular establishes a mandatory three-stage credit facility classification framework for all scheduled commercial banks. Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.
executive_summary.background: Issued under powers conferred by the Bank Company Act, 1991 to strengthen risk management in the banking sector.
executive_summary.purpose: Harmonization of credit risk measurement with international accounting standard IFRS 9.
key_changes: Introduction of mandatory 3-stage credit classification framework
Mandatory general provision of 5.00% on Stage 2 underperforming loans
Ban on interest reversal into income without prior written approval from Bangladesh Bank

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk since initial recognition. General provision of 1.00% must be maintained.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: Stage 2 (Underperforming): Loans exhibiting significant increase in credit risk (SICR) or overdue past 30 days up to 89 days. General provision of 5.00% must be maintained.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: The amended provisions set forth in this Circular shall come into force with effect from 01 January 2025. All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.title: Maintain 5.00% General Provision on Stage 2 Loans
obligations.requirement_description: Scheduled commercial banks must maintain 5.00% general provisioning on credit facilities categorized under Stage 2 (overdue 30-89 days).
obligations.verbatim_quote: Stage 2 (Underperforming): Loans exhibiting significant increase in credit risk (SICR) or overdue past 30 days up to 89 days. General provision of 5.00% must be maintained.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.title: Submit Initial IFRS 9 Readiness Report
obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.
obligations.verbatim_quote: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All scheduled commercial banks
obligations.required_evidence: Board-approved IFRS 9 transition readiness report
obligations.consequence: Supervisory warning and inspection scrutiny

exemptions: Islamic Banks are covered under separate shariah-compliant guidelines
applicability.conditional_rules: Applies to all loan portfolios exceeding initial recognition

deadlines.trigger_event: Circular publication on Bangladesh Bank website

relationships.supporting_quote: Please refer to BRPD Circular No. 14 dated 23 September 2012 and subsequent instructions issued on loan classification and provisioning standards for scheduled commercial banks.

impact_assessment.banking_operations: Requires core banking system loan staging automation.
impact_assessment.credit: Increased provisioning buffer required for Stage 2 loans.
impact_assessment.risk_management: Model calibration for Significant Increase in Credit Risk (SICR).

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank introduces a master policy aligning loan classification and general provisioning standards with IFRS 9.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: The circular establishes a mandatory three-stage credit facility classification framework for all scheduled commercial banks. Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.
executive_summary.background: Issued under powers conferred by the Bank Company Act, 1991 to strengthen risk management in the banking sector.
executive_summary.purpose: Harmonization of credit risk measurement with international accounting standard IFRS 9.

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk since initial recognition. General provision of 1.00% must be maintained.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: Stage 2 (Underperforming): Loans exhibiting significant increase in credit risk (SICR) or overdue past 30 days up to 89 days. General provision of 5.00% must be maintained.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: The amended provisions set forth in this Circular shall come into force with effect from 01 January 2025. All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.title: Maintain 5.00% General Provision on Stage 2 Loans
obligations.requirement_description: Scheduled commercial banks must maintain 5.00% general provisioning on credit facilities categorized under Stage 2 (overdue 30-89 days).
obligations.verbatim_quote: Stage 2 (Underperforming): Loans exhibiting significant increase in credit risk (SICR) or overdue past 30 days up to 89 days. General provision of 5.00% must be maintained.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.title: Submit Initial IFRS 9 Readiness Report
obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.
obligations.verbatim_quote: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All scheduled commercial banks
obligations.required_evidence: Board-approved IFRS 9 transition readiness report
obligations.consequence: Supervisory warning and inspection scrutiny

exemptions: Islamic Banks are covered under separate shariah-compliant guidelines
applicability.conditional_rules: Applies to all loan portfolios exceeding initial recognition

classification.subject: Master Policy on Loan Classification and Provisioning Alignment with IFRS 9

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank introduces a master policy aligning loan classification and general provisioning standards with IFRS 9.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: The circular establishes a mandatory three-stage credit facility classification framework for all scheduled commercial banks. Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.
executive_summary.background: Issued under powers conferred by the Bank Company Act, 1991 to strengthen risk management in the banking sector.
executive_summary.purpose: Harmonization of credit risk measurement with international accounting standard IFRS 9.
key_changes: Introduction of mandatory 3-stage credit classification framework
Mandatory general provision of 5.00% on Stage 2 underperforming loans
Ban on interest reversal into income without prior written approval from Bangladesh Bank

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.title: Maintain 5.00% General Provision on Stage 2 Loans
obligations.requirement_description: Scheduled commercial banks must maintain 5.00% general provisioning on credit facilities categorized under Stage 2 (overdue 30-89 days).
obligations.verbatim_quote: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.title: Submit Initial IFRS 9 Readiness Report
obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.
obligations.verbatim_quote: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All scheduled commercial banks
obligations.required_evidence: Board-approved IFRS 9 transition readiness report
obligations.consequence: Supervisory warning and inspection scrutiny

exemptions: Islamic Banks are covered under separate shariah-compliant guidelines
applicability.conditional_rules: Applies to all loan portfolios exceeding initial recognition

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank introduces a master policy aligning loan classification and general provisioning standards with IFRS 9.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: The circular establishes a mandatory three-stage credit facility classification framework for all scheduled commercial banks.
