provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.
executive_summary.background: Issued under powers conferred by the Bank Company Act, 1991 to strengthen risk management in the banking sector.
executive_summary.purpose: Harmonization of credit risk measurement with international accounting standard IFRS 9.
key_changes: Introduction of mandatory 3-stage credit classification framework
Mandatory general provision of 5.00% on Stage 2 underperforming loans
Ban on interest reversal into income without prior written approval from Bangladesh Bank

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.title: Maintain 5.00% General Provision on Stage 2 Loans
obligations.requirement_description: Scheduled commercial banks must maintain 5.00% general provisioning on credit facilities categorized under Stage 2 (overdue 30-89 days).
obligations.verbatim_quote: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.title: Submit Initial IFRS 9 Readiness Report
obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.
obligations.verbatim_quote: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All scheduled commercial banks
obligations.required_evidence: Board-approved IFRS 9 transition readiness report
obligations.consequence: Supervisory warning and inspection scrutiny

exemptions: Islamic Banks are covered under separate shariah-compliant guidelines
applicability.conditional_rules: Applies to all loan portfolios exceeding initial recognition

classification.subject: Master Policy on Loan Classification and Provisioning Alignment with IFRS 9

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank introduces a master policy aligning loan classification and general provisioning standards with IFRS 9.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: The circular establishes a mandatory three-stage credit facility classification framework for all scheduled commercial banks. Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.
executive_summary.background: Issued under powers conferred by the Bank Company Act, 1991 to strengthen risk management in the banking sector.
executive_summary.purpose: Harmonization of credit risk measurement with international accounting standard IFRS 9.
key_changes: Introduction of mandatory 3-stage credit classification framework
Mandatory general provision of 5.00% on Stage 2 underperforming loans
Ban on interest reversal into income without prior written approval from Bangladesh Bank

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.title: Maintain 5.00% General Provision on Stage 2 Loans
obligations.requirement_description: Scheduled commercial banks must maintain 5.00% general provisioning on credit facilities categorized under Stage 2 (overdue 30-89 days).
obligations.verbatim_quote: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.title: Submit Initial IFRS 9 Readiness Report
obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.
obligations.verbatim_quote: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All scheduled commercial banks
obligations.required_evidence: Board-approved IFRS 9 transition readiness report
obligations.consequence: Supervisory warning and inspection scrutiny

exemptions: Islamic Banks are covered under separate shariah-compliant guidelines
applicability.conditional_rules: Applies to all loan portfolios exceeding initial recognition

classification.subject: Master Policy on Loan Classification and Provisioning Alignment with IFRS 9

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank introduces a master policy aligning loan classification and general provisioning standards with IFRS 9.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: The circular establishes a mandatory three-stage credit facility classification framework for all scheduled commercial banks. Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.
executive_summary.background: Issued under powers conferred by the Bank Company Act, 1991 to strengthen risk management in the banking sector.
executive_summary.purpose: Harmonization of credit risk measurement with international accounting standard IFRS 9.
key_changes: Introduction of mandatory 3-stage credit classification framework
Mandatory general provision of 5.00% on Stage 2 underperforming loans
Ban on interest reversal into income without prior written approval from Bangladesh Bank

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.title: Maintain 5.00% General Provision on Stage 2 Loans

obligations.verbatim_quote: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.

obligations.applicability_conditions: All scheduled commercial banks
obligations.required_evidence: Board-approved IFRS 9 transition readiness report
obligations.consequence: Supervisory warning and inspection scrutiny

provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.title: Maintain 5.00% General Provision on Stage 2 Loans
obligations.requirement_description: Scheduled commercial banks must maintain 5.00% general provisioning on credit facilities categorized under Stage 2 (overdue 30-89 days).
obligations.verbatim_quote: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.title: Submit Initial IFRS 9 Readiness Report
obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.
obligations.verbatim_quote: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All scheduled commercial banks
obligations.required_evidence: Board-approved IFRS 9 transition readiness report
obligations.consequence: Supervisory warning and inspection scrutiny

Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days

obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.title: Submit Initial IFRS 9 Readiness Report
obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.

classification.subject: Master Policy on Loan Classification and Provisioning Alignment with IFRS 9

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank introduces a master policy aligning loan classification and general provisioning standards with IFRS 9.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: The circular establishes a mandatory three-stage credit facility classification framework for all scheduled commercial banks. Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.
executive_summary.background: Issued under powers conferred by the Bank Company Act, 1991 to strengthen risk management in the banking sector.
executive_summary.purpose: Harmonization of credit risk measurement with international accounting standard IFRS 9.
key_changes: Introduction of mandatory 3-stage credit classification framework
Mandatory general provision of 5.00% on Stage 2 underperforming loans
Ban on interest reversal into income without prior written approval from Bangladesh Bank

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.title: Maintain 5.00% General Provision on Stage 2 Loans
obligations.requirement_description: Scheduled commercial banks must maintain 5.00% general provisioning on credit facilities categorized under Stage 2 (overdue 30-89 days).
obligations.verbatim_quote: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.title: Submit Initial IFRS 9 Readiness Report
obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.
obligations.verbatim_quote: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All scheduled commercial banks
obligations.required_evidence: Board-approved IFRS 9 transition readiness report
obligations.consequence: Supervisory warning and inspection scrutiny

exemptions: Islamic Banks are covered under separate shariah-compliant guidelines
applicability.conditional_rules: Applies to all loan portfolios exceeding initial recognition

deadlines.trigger_event: Circular publication on Bangladesh Bank website

relationships.supporting_quote: Please refer to BRPD Circular No. 14 dated 23 September 2012 and subsequent instructions issued on loan classification and provisioning standards for scheduled commercial banks.

impact_assessment.credit: Increased provisioning buffer required for Stage 2 loans.

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank introduces a master policy aligning loan classification and general provisioning standards with IFRS 9.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: The circular establishes a mandatory three-stage credit facility classification framework for all scheduled commercial banks. Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

executive_summary.detailed_summary: The circular establishes a mandatory three-stage credit facility classification framework for all scheduled commercial banks. Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.
executive_summary.background: Issued under powers conferred by the Bank Company Act, 1991 to strengthen risk management in the banking sector.
executive_summary.purpose: Harmonization of credit risk measurement with international accounting standard IFRS 9.
key_changes: Introduction of mandatory 3-stage credit classification framework
Mandatory general provision of 5.00% on Stage 2 underperforming loans
Ban on interest reversal into income without prior written approval from Bangladesh Bank

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.title: Maintain 5.00% General Provision on Stage 2 Loans
obligations.requirement_description: Scheduled commercial banks must maintain 5.00% general provisioning on credit facilities categorized under Stage 2 (overdue 30-89 days).
obligations.verbatim_quote: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.title: Submit Initial IFRS 9 Readiness Report
obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.
obligations.verbatim_quote: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All scheduled commercial banks
obligations.required_evidence: Board-approved IFRS 9 transition readiness report
obligations.consequence: Supervisory warning and inspection scrutiny

exemptions: Islamic Banks are covered under separate shariah-compliant guidelines
applicability.conditional_rules: Applies to all loan portfolios exceeding initial recognition

deadlines.trigger_event: Circular publication on Bangladesh Bank website

relationships.supporting_quote: Please refer to BRPD Circular No. 14 dated 23 September 2012 and subsequent instructions issued on loan classification and provisioning standards for scheduled commercial banks.

impact_assessment.banking_operations: Requires core banking system loan staging automation.
impact_assessment.credit: Increased provisioning buffer required for Stage 2 loans.
impact_assessment.risk_management: Model calibration for Significant Increase in Credit Risk (SICR).

classification.subject: Master Policy on Loan Classification and Provisioning Alignment with IFRS 9

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank introduces a master policy aligning loan classification and general provisioning standards with IFRS 9.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: The circular establishes a mandatory three-stage credit facility classification framework for all scheduled commercial banks. Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.
executive_summary.background: Issued under powers conferred by the Bank Company Act, 1991 to strengthen risk management in the banking sector.
executive_summary.purpose: Harmonization of credit risk measurement with international accounting standard IFRS 9.
key_changes: Introduction of mandatory 3-stage credit classification framework
Mandatory general provision of 5.00% on Stage 2 underperforming loans
Ban on interest reversal into income without prior written approval from Bangladesh Bank

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.title: Maintain 5.00% General Provision on Stage 2 Loans
obligations.requirement_description: Scheduled commercial banks must maintain 5.00% general provisioning on credit facilities categorized under Stage 2 (overdue 30-89 days).
obligations.verbatim_quote: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.title: Submit Initial IFRS 9 Readiness Report
obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.
obligations.verbatim_quote: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All scheduled commercial banks
obligations.required_evidence: Board-approved IFRS 9 transition readiness report
obligations.consequence: Supervisory warning and inspection scrutiny

exemptions: Islamic Banks are covered under separate shariah-compliant guidelines
applicability.conditional_rules: Applies to all loan portfolios exceeding initial recognition

classification.subject: Master Policy on Loan Classification and Provisioning Alignment with IFRS 9

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank introduces a master policy aligning loan classification and general provisioning standards with IFRS 9.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: The circular establishes a mandatory three-stage credit facility classification framework for all scheduled commercial banks. Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.
executive_summary.background: Issued under powers conferred by the Bank Company Act, 1991 to strengthen risk management in the banking sector.
executive_summary.purpose: Harmonization of credit risk measurement with international accounting standard IFRS 9.
key_changes: Introduction of mandatory 3-stage credit classification framework
Mandatory general provision of 5.00% on Stage 2 underperforming loans
Ban on interest reversal into income without prior written approval from Bangladesh Bank

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.title: Maintain 5.00% General Provision on Stage 2 Loans
obligations.requirement_description: Scheduled commercial banks must maintain 5.00% general provisioning on credit facilities categorized under Stage 2 (overdue 30-89 days).
obligations.verbatim_quote: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.title: Submit Initial IFRS 9 Readiness Report
obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.
obligations.verbatim_quote: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All scheduled commercial banks
obligations.required_evidence: Board-approved IFRS 9 transition readiness report
obligations.consequence: Supervisory warning and inspection scrutiny

exemptions: Islamic Banks are covered under separate shariah-compliant guidelines
applicability.conditional_rules: Applies to all loan portfolios exceeding initial recognition

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days

obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

classification.subject: Master Policy on Loan Classification and Provisioning Alignment with IFRS 9

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank introduces a master policy aligning loan classification and general provisioning standards with IFRS 9.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: The circular establishes a mandatory three-stage credit facility classification framework for all scheduled commercial banks. Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.
executive_summary.background: Issued under powers conferred by the Bank Company Act, 1991 to strengthen risk management in the banking sector.
executive_summary.purpose: Harmonization of credit risk measurement with international accounting standard IFRS 9.
key_changes: Introduction of mandatory 3-stage credit classification framework
Mandatory general provision of 5.00% on Stage 2 underperforming loans
Ban on interest reversal into income without prior written approval from Bangladesh Bank

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.title: Maintain 5.00% General Provision on Stage 2 Loans
obligations.requirement_description: Scheduled commercial banks must maintain 5.00% general provisioning on credit facilities categorized under Stage 2 (overdue 30-89 days).
obligations.verbatim_quote: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.title: Submit Initial IFRS 9 Readiness Report
obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.
obligations.verbatim_quote: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All scheduled commercial banks
obligations.required_evidence: Board-approved IFRS 9 transition readiness report
obligations.consequence: Supervisory warning and inspection scrutiny

exemptions: Islamic Banks are covered under separate shariah-compliant guidelines
applicability.conditional_rules: Applies to all loan portfolios exceeding initial recognition

deadlines.trigger_event: Circular publication on Bangladesh Bank website

relationships.supporting_quote: Please refer to BRPD Circular No. 14 dated 23 September 2012 and subsequent instructions issued on loan classification and provisioning standards for scheduled commercial banks.

impact_assessment.credit: Increased provisioning buffer required for Stage 2 loans.
impact_assessment.risk_management: Model calibration for Significant Increase in Credit Risk (SICR).

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank introduces a master policy aligning loan classification and general provisioning standards with IFRS 9.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: The circular establishes a mandatory three-stage credit facility classification framework for all scheduled commercial banks. provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.
executive_summary.background: Issued under powers conferred by the Bank Company Act, 1991 to strengthen risk management in the banking sector.
executive_summary.purpose: Harmonization of credit risk measurement with international accounting standard IFRS 9.
key_changes: Introduction of mandatory 3-stage credit classification framework
Mandatory general provision of 5.00% on Stage 2 underperforming loans
Ban on interest reversal into income without prior written approval from Bangladesh Bank

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.title: Maintain 5.00% General Provision on Stage 2 Loans
obligations.requirement_description: Scheduled commercial banks must maintain 5.00% general provisioning on credit facilities categorized under Stage 2 (overdue 30-89 days).
obligations.verbatim_quote: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.title: Submit Initial IFRS 9 Readiness Report
obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.
obligations.verbatim_quote: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All scheduled commercial banks
obligations.required_evidence: Board-approved IFRS 9 transition readiness report
obligations.consequence: Supervisory warning and inspection scrutiny

exemptions: Islamic Banks are covered under separate shariah-compliant guidelines
applicability.conditional_rules: Applies to all loan portfolios exceeding initial recognition

classification.subject: Master Policy on Loan Classification and Provisioning Alignment with IFRS 9

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank introduces a master policy aligning loan classification and general provisioning standards with IFRS 9.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: The circular establishes a mandatory three-stage credit facility classification framework for all scheduled commercial banks. Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.
executive_summary.background: Issued under powers conferred by the Bank Company Act, 1991 to strengthen risk management in the banking sector.
executive_summary.purpose: Harmonization of credit risk measurement with international accounting standard IFRS 9.
key_changes: Introduction of mandatory 3-stage credit classification framework
Mandatory general provision of 5.00% on Stage 2 underperforming loans
Ban on interest reversal into income without prior written approval from Bangladesh Bank

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.title: Maintain 5.00% General Provision on Stage 2 Loans
obligations.requirement_description: Scheduled commercial banks must maintain 5.00% general provisioning on credit facilities categorized under Stage 2 (overdue 30-89 days).
obligations.verbatim_quote: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.title: Submit Initial IFRS 9 Readiness Report
obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.
obligations.verbatim_quote: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All scheduled commercial banks
obligations.required_evidence: Board-approved IFRS 9 transition readiness report
obligations.consequence: Supervisory warning and inspection scrutiny

exemptions: Islamic Banks are covered under separate shariah-compliant guidelines
applicability.conditional_rules: Applies to all loan portfolios exceeding initial recognition

classification.subject: Master Policy on Loan Classification and Provisioning Alignment with IFRS 9

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank introduces a master policy aligning loan classification and general provisioning standards with IFRS 9.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: The circular establishes a mandatory three-stage credit facility classification framework for all scheduled commercial banks. Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.
executive_summary.background: Issued under powers conferred by the Bank Company Act, 1991 to strengthen risk management in the banking sector.
executive_summary.purpose: Harmonization of credit risk measurement with international accounting standard IFRS 9.
key_changes: Introduction of mandatory 3-stage credit classification framework
Mandatory general provision of 5.00% on Stage 2 underperforming loans
Ban on interest reversal into income without prior written approval from Bangladesh Bank

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.title: Maintain 5.00% General Provision on Stage 2 Loans

obligations.verbatim_quote: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.

obligations.applicability_conditions: All scheduled commercial banks
obligations.required_evidence: Board-approved IFRS 9 transition readiness report
obligations.consequence: Supervisory warning and inspection scrutiny

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.

classification.subject: Master Policy on Loan Classification and Provisioning Alignment with IFRS 9

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank introduces a master policy aligning loan classification and general provisioning standards with IFRS 9.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: The circular establishes a mandatory three-stage credit facility classification framework for all scheduled commercial banks. Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.
executive_summary.background: Issued under powers conferred by the Bank Company Act, 1991 to strengthen risk management in the banking sector.
executive_summary.purpose: Harmonization of credit risk measurement with international accounting standard IFRS 9.
key_changes: Introduction of mandatory 3-stage credit classification framework
Mandatory general provision of 5.00% on Stage 2 underperforming loans
Ban on interest reversal into income without prior written approval from Bangladesh Bank

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.title: Maintain 5.00% General Provision on Stage 2 Loans
obligations.requirement_description: Scheduled commercial banks must maintain 5.00% general provisioning on credit facilities categorized under Stage 2 (overdue 30-89 days).
obligations.verbatim_quote: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.title: Submit Initial IFRS 9 Readiness Report
obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.
obligations.verbatim_quote: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All scheduled commercial banks
obligations.required_evidence: Board-approved IFRS 9 transition readiness report
obligations.consequence: Supervisory warning and inspection scrutiny

exemptions: Islamic Banks are covered under separate shariah-compliant guidelines
applicability.conditional_rules: Applies to all loan portfolios exceeding initial recognition

classification.subject: Master Policy on Loan Classification and Provisioning Alignment with IFRS 9

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank introduces a master policy aligning loan classification and general provisioning standards with IFRS 9.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: The circular establishes a mandatory three-stage credit facility classification framework for all scheduled commercial banks. Stage 1 requires 1.00% general provision, Stage 2 requires 5.00% provision, and Stage 3 requires specific provisioning for non-performing loans.
executive_summary.background: Issued under powers conferred by the Bank Company Act, 1991 to strengthen risk management in the banking sector.
executive_summary.purpose: Harmonization of credit risk measurement with international accounting standard IFRS 9.
key_changes: Introduction of mandatory 3-stage credit classification framework
Mandatory general provision of 5.00% on Stage 2 underperforming loans
Ban on interest reversal into income without prior written approval from Bangladesh Bank

provisions.heading: Mandatory Staging Framework
provisions.verbatim_text: All scheduled commercial banks must classify their credit facilities into three distinct stages:
provisions.normalized_explanation: Mandates 3-stage loan classification for all scheduled banks.

provisions.heading: Stage 1 Performing
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.1 Stage 1 (Performing): Loans with no significant increase in credit risk. General provision: 1.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 1 requires 1% general provision.

provisions.heading: Stage 2 Underperforming
provisions.verbatim_text: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Stage 2 loans overdue 30-89 days require 5% general provision.

provisions.heading: Effective Date & Compliance Timeline
provisions.verbatim_text: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Enforceable from Jan 1, 2025 with readiness report due Dec 31, 2024.

provisions.heading: Penal Sanctions
provisions.verbatim_text: Failure to comply with these provisions will attract penal actions under Section 109(7) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Penal consequences under Bank Company Act Section 109(7).

obligations.title: Maintain 5.00% General Provision on Stage 2 Loans
obligations.requirement_description: Scheduled commercial banks must maintain 5.00% general provisioning on credit facilities categorized under Stage 2 (overdue 30-89 days).
obligations.verbatim_quote: 1.2 Stage 2 (Underperforming): Significant increase in credit risk (overdue 30-89 days). Provision: 5.00%.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All credit facilities with significant increase in credit risk overdue 30 to 89 days
obligations.required_evidence: Quarterly CL-1/CL-2 regulatory reporting submission to BRPD and statutory audit confirmation
obligations.consequence: Penal sanctions under Section 109(7) of Bank Company Act, 1991

obligations.title: Submit Initial IFRS 9 Readiness Report
obligations.requirement_description: Submit comprehensive readiness report outlining IT readiness and model calibration to BRPD.
obligations.verbatim_quote: All banks must submit an initial readiness report to BRPD within 31 December 2024.
obligations.applicability_conditions: All scheduled commercial banks
obligations.required_evidence: Board-approved IFRS 9 transition readiness report
obligations.consequence: Supervisory warning and inspection scrutiny

exemptions: Islamic Banks are covered under separate shariah-compliant guidelines
applicability.conditional_rules: Applies to all loan portfolios exceeding initial recognition

document_analyses.executive_summary: Bangladesh Bank issued a circular letter extending eligibility for the SME working capital refinancing fund to all finance companies operating in Bangladesh.
document_analyses.purpose: To extend SME working capital refinancing fund eligibility to all finance companies operating in Bangladesh and ensure compliance with specified regulatory conditions.
document_analyses.background: The directive references prior circulars and circular letters issued by the SME and Special Programmes Department, notably SMESPD Circular No. 04 dated 08 June 2026, SMESPD Circular No. 01 dated 17 March 2025, and SMESPD Circular Letter No. 02 dated 12 November 2025.
key_changes: Finance companies operating in Bangladesh are declared eligible to receive refinancing under the SME working capital refinancing fund.

Mandated compliance with paragraph 14.4.2 of SMESPD Circular No. 01 (dated 17 March 2025) and paragraph 2 of SMESPD Circular Letter No. 02 (dated 12 November 2025) to achieve participating institution eligibility.

impact_summary.credit: Expands credit access for SMEs by allowing finance companies to participate in the working capital refinancing fund.
impact_summary.compliance: Finance companies must align their eligibility processes with the conditions stipulated in SMESPD Circular No. 01 and SMESPD Circular Letter No. 02.

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank issued a circular letter extending eligibility for the SME working capital refinancing fund to all finance companies operating in Bangladesh.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: This circular letter clarifies that all finance companies operating in Bangladesh are eligible to receive refinancing under the SME working capital refinancing fund, subject to fulfilling prior compliance requirements stipulated in SMESPD Circular No. 01 dated 17 March 2025 and SMESPD Circular Letter No. 02 dated 12 November 2025. Furthermore, all other instructions outlined in SMESPD Circular No. 04 dated 08 June 2026 shall apply to the finance companies. The directive is issued under the powers conferred by Section 41 of the Finance Company Act, 2023.

provisions.verbatim_text: বাংলাদেশে কাযর্রত সকল ফাইন্যান্স কোম্পানি আলোচ্য সাকুর্লারের আওতায় পুনঃ অথার্য়ন গ্রহণের যোগ্য বলে বিবেচিত হবে। সেÿেত্রে, অংশগ্রহণকারী প্রতিষ্ঠান হিসেবে যোগ্যতা অজের্ন ফাইন্যান্স কোম্পানিসমূহকে এসএমইএসপিডি সাকুর্লার নং-০১, তারিখ-১৭ মাচর্ ২০২৫ এর ১৪.৪.২ নং অনুচ্ছেদ ও এসএমইএসপিডি সাকুর্লার লেটার নং-০২, তারিখ ১২ নভেম্বর ২০২৫ এর ২ নং অনুচ্ছেদের শতর্ পরিপালন করতে হবে।

document_analyses.executive_summary: Bangladesh Bank has instructed all scheduled banks to keep their branches open on Saturday, December 27, 2025, to facilitate the deposit of nomination security funds and voter list CD purchase fees for the 13th National Parliamentary Election.

document_analyses.background: Issued upon the request of the Bangladesh Election Commission Secretariat memo dated 24 December 2025, and utilizing statutory powers under Section 45 of the Bank Company Act, 1991.

impact_summary.technology: IT and payment systems (for pay orders, bank drafts, and challans) must be operational.

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank has instructed all scheduled banks to keep their branches open on Saturday, December 27, 2025, to facilitate the deposit of nomination security funds and voter list CD purchase fees for the 13th National Parliamentary Election.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: Pursuant to a letter from the Bangladesh Election Commission Secretariat, Bangladesh Bank issued a circular letter mandating all scheduled banks operating in Bangladesh to keep all their branches open on Saturday, December 27, 2025. This measure is intended to facilitate candidates in depositing money for nomination security and purchasing voter list CDs through bank drafts, pay orders, or treasury challans for the upcoming 13th National Parliamentary Election. The directive is issued under the authority vested in Bangladesh Bank via Section 45 of the Bank Company Act, 1991 in the public interest.

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank issued an exemption for United Commercial Bank PLC from the shareholding limit under section 14K(1) of the Bank Company Act, 1991, allowing up to 30% shareholding.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: Through Circular Letter No. 17 and an enclosed notification (No-BRPD-2(R-1)(Law Review)717/2026-4375), Bangladesh Bank has granted an exemption to United Commercial Bank PLC under the powers given in section 121 of the Bank Company Act, 1991. To strengthen the capital structure of United Commercial Bank PLC, individuals, institutions, companies, or family members (directly or indirectly, singly or jointly) are permitted to hold up to a maximum of 30 percent of the paid-up capital of the bank, thereby exempting it from the restriction outlined in section 14K(1) of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
executive_summary.background: The notification is issued using powers conferred under section 121 of the Bank Company Act, 1991 (Act No. 14 of 1991) to strengthen the capital structure of United Commercial Bank PLC.
executive_summary.purpose: To strengthen the capital structure of United Commercial Bank PLC by permitting higher shareholding limits.
key_changes: Exemption from section 14K(1) of the Bank Company Act, 1991 for United Commercial Bank PLC.
Permission for any person, institution, company, or family members to hold up to a maximum of 30% of the paid-up capital of United Commercial Bank PLC.

document_analyses.executive_summary: Bangladesh Bank issued comprehensive guidelines regarding the issuance, conversion, redemption, and dividend repatriation of preference shares for non-resident investors.
document_analyses.purpose: To regulate and streamline the issuance, redemption, and conversion of preference shares in favour of non-resident investors, as well as the repatriation of dividends thereon, addressing their distinctive features compared to ordinary shares.
document_analyses.background: Issued pursuant to Paragraph 2(A), Chapter 9, Guidelines for Foreign Exchange Transactions, 2018 (GFET-2018), Vol. 1, FEID Circular No. 01 dated 27 January 2025, and FEID Circular No. 01 dated 08 March 2026, under the authority conferred by Section 20(3) of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA), 1947.
key_changes: Preference shares may be issued by resident manufacturing or service sector companies to non-resident investors subject to Companies Act, BSEC rules, and MoA/AoA.
Issuance must be against foreign currency remitted through official banking channels.
No prior BB approval is required if the dividend rate does not exceed 5% of face value; other rates require FEID approval via an AD bank.
AD banks must report issuance within 14 days and post facto report redemption instalments within 30 days.
Fully convertible and irredeemable preference shares shall be treated as equity capital.

impact_summary.banking_operations: AD banks must process preference share issuance reporting within 14 days, post-facto redemption reporting within 30 days, maintain year-wise repatriation records, and preserve TDS/NBR documentation.
impact_summary.compliance: Mandates strict adherence to KYC, AML/CFT standards, tax laws, BSEC regulations, and Companies Act provisions for preference share transactions.
impact_summary.risk_management: Ensures foreign currency remittances through official banking channels and prevents claims for interest or compensation on unrepatriated principal or dividends past due dates.

classification.subject: Issuance, conversion and redemption of preference shares in favour of non-resident investors and repatriation of dividends thereon
classification.regulatory_topic: Foreign Exchange Investment and Preference Shares

executive_summary.short_summary: Bangladesh Bank issued comprehensive guidelines regarding the issuance, conversion, redemption, and dividend repatriation of preference shares for non-resident investors.
executive_summary.detailed_summary: This circular outlines the regulatory framework for Bangladeshi resident companies in manufacturing or service sectors issuing preference shares to non-resident investors. It covers funding requirements, subscription agreements, dividend rates and approvals, reporting obligations for Authorized Dealer (AD) banks, valuation for conversion, repatriation of dividends and redemption proceeds, and compliance with KYC, AML/CFT, and tax laws.
executive_summary.background: Issued pursuant to Paragraph 2(A), Chapter 9, Guidelines for Foreign Exchange Transactions, 2018 (GFET-2018), Vol. 1, FEID Circular No. 01 dated 27 January 2025, and FEID Circular No. 01 dated 08 March 2026, under the authority conferred by Section 20(3) of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA), 1947.
executive_summary.purpose: To regulate and streamline the issuance, redemption, and conversion of preference shares in favour of non-resident investors, as well as the repatriation of dividends thereon, addressing their distinctive features compared to ordinary shares.
key_changes: Preference shares may be issued by resident manufacturing or service sector companies to non-resident investors subject to Companies Act, BSEC rules, and MoA/AoA.
Issuance must be against foreign currency remitted through official banking channels.
No prior BB approval is required if the dividend rate does not exceed 5% of face value; other rates require FEID approval via an AD bank.
AD banks must report issuance within 14 days and post facto report redemption instalments within 30 days.
Fully convertible and irredeemable preference shares shall be treated as equity capital.
affected_stakeholders: Authorized Dealers (AD) in Foreign Exchange in Bangladesh
Bangladeshi resident companies in manufacturing or service sectors

provisions.verbatim_text: Any Bangladeshi resident company operating in the manufacturing or service sector may issue preference shares in favour of non-resident investors, subject to the provisions of the Companies Act, 1994, the applicable rules and regulations of the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (BSEC), and the company's Memorandum and Articles of Association (MoA and AoA).
provisions.normalized_explanation: Resident companies in manufacturing or services can issue preference shares to non-residents following the Companies Act, BSEC regulations, and their own MoA and AoA.

provisions.verbatim_text: Preference shares shall be issued only against foreign currency remitted into Bangladesh through official banking channels.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Payment for preference shares must originate from foreign currency sent via official banking channels.

provisions.verbatim_text: A subscription agreement between the resident company and the non-resident investor for the issuance of preference shares shall be executed, subject to Bangladesh Bank’s authorization where required under this circular. The agreement shall clearly specify the number of preference shares to be issued, their face value and issue price denominated in Bangladeshi Taka (BDT), the dividend rate, and the terms and conditions governing the preference shares, including their tenure, redemption and conversion features, as applicable.
provisions.normalized_explanation: A subscription agreement must be executed detailing share counts, BDT face value and price, dividend rate, tenure, and conversion/redemption terms.

provisions.verbatim_text: No prior approval from Bangladesh Bank shall be required where the dividend rate on preference shares does not exceed 5% of their face value. In all other cases, including preference shares carrying participating or adjustable dividend rates, an application, together with proper justification for the proposed dividend rate, shall be submitted to FEID of Bangladesh Bank, through the nominated Authorized Dealer (AD) bank for consideration and approval.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Dividend rates up to 5% do not need prior Bangladesh Bank approval; higher or variable rates require application through the AD bank.

provisions.verbatim_text: AD banks shall report the issuance of preference shares to the FEID, Bangladesh Bank, within 14 (fourteen) days of such issuance, together with all relevant supporting documents, including the company's Memorandum and Articles of Association (MoA and AoA), Form XV (Return of Allotment) duly endorsed by the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms (RJSC), an Encashment Certificate in the prescribed format (Appendix 5/39 or 5/40) indicating the Online Foreign Exchange (FX) Transaction ID, and Schedule X, where applicable.
provisions.normalized_explanation: AD banks must report share issuances to FEID within 14 days with supporting documents like MoA/AoA, RJSC-endorsed Form XV, Encashment Certificate, and Schedule X.

provisions.verbatim_text: Preference shares shall be issued at par, and accordingly, valuation of the company shall not be required for the issuance or redemption of such shares. However, where preference shares carry a conversion feature, the fair value of the ordinary shares shall be determined in accordance with the methodology prescribed in FEID Circular No. 01 dated 8 March 2026 for the purpose of determining the applicable conversion ratio.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Preference shares must be issued at par without company valuation, but conversion requires determining ordinary share fair value based on FEID Circular No. 01 of 8 March 2026.

provisions.verbatim_text: Upon conversion of preference shares into ordinary shares, the issuing company shall, through its AD bank, notify FEID of Bangladesh Bank, and submit the relevant supporting documents as prescribed in paragraph 2(A), chapter 9 of GFET-2018, Vol.1.
provisions.normalized_explanation: The issuing company, via its AD bank, must notify FEID and submit documents upon converting preference shares to ordinary shares.

provisions.verbatim_text: Where preference shares have been issued in compliance with the provisions of this circular, the nominated AD bank may remit dividends and redemption proceeds to non-resident investors without prior approval from Bangladesh Bank, subject to compliance of the relevant provisions of foreign exchange regulations; and deduction and payment of applicable taxes. However, in respect of each remittance of a redemption instalment, AD bank shall submit a post facto report to the Foreign Exchange Investment Department (FEID), Bangladesh Bank, within 30 (thirty) days from the date of remittance, together with the relevant supporting documents, including the TM Form bearing the Online Foreign Exchange (FX) Transaction ID.
provisions.normalized_explanation: AD banks may remit compliant dividends and redemptions without prior BB approval, provided taxes are paid, but must submit post-facto redemption reports within 30 days.

provisions.verbatim_text: Dividends and redemption proceeds shall be repatriated through AD bank through which the original capital funds were remitted into Bangladesh. AD bank shall maintain year-wise records of all dividends and redemption proceeds repatriated to non-resident investors.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Repatriation must go through the original AD bank, which must keep year-wise records of all repatriations.

provisions.verbatim_text: Dividends and redemption proceeds shall be repatriated to the non-resident investor in the country from which the original investment funds were remitted into Bangladesh.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Repatriations must be sent back to the same country from which original investment funds came.

provisions.verbatim_text: If any principal amount or accrued dividends remain unrepatriated after the due date of any instalment or upon expiry of the term of the preference shares, as applicable, no further interest or compensation shall be payable or claimable in respect of such outstanding amounts.
provisions.normalized_explanation: No further interest or compensation can be claimed for unrepatriated principal or dividends after due dates or expiry.

provisions.verbatim_text: Dividends on preference shares may be reinvested in ordinary shares of the same company or another company at their respective fair values.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Preference share dividends can be reinvested into ordinary shares at fair value.

provisions.verbatim_text: AD bank shall preserve the auditor’s certificate supporting the calculation of Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) and the amount eligible for repatriation. Where applicable, the relevant documents issued by the National Board of Revenue (NBR) for the purposes of availing benefits under a Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) shall also be obtained and maintained in the respective file. All relevant documents shall be properly maintained by AD bank and made readily available for inspection by Bangladesh Bank officials upon request.
provisions.normalized_explanation: AD banks must preserve auditor TDS certificates, NBR DTAA documents, and maintain them for BB inspection.

provisions.verbatim_text: Any change in the nominated AD bank shall be subject to obtaining a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the existing AD bank. All relevant records relating to dividends repatriated shall be duly transferred to the newly appointed AD bank. Any such change shall also be duly notified to the FEID, Bangladesh Bank.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Changing the nominated AD bank requires an NOC from the current bank, transfer of records, and notification to FEID.

provisions.verbatim_text: In the event of redemption of preference shares, AD bank shall submit to FEID of Bangladesh Bank, two copies of Schedule X: the first immediately before the payment date of the final redemption instalment, and the second following such payment, reflecting the removal of the preference shareholders’ names. AD bank shall also submit the corresponding financial statements for both periods.
provisions.normalized_explanation: For share redemptions, AD banks must submit Schedule X twice (before final payment and after removal of names) along with financial statements.

provisions.verbatim_text: Fully convertible and irredeemable preference shares shall be treated as equity capital.
provisions.normalized_explanation: Fully convertible and irredeemable preference shares qualify as equity capital.

provisions.verbatim_text: AD banks shall ensure compliance with applicable KYC requirements, AML/CFT standards, tax laws, and all other relevant laws, rules, regulations, and regulatory requirements.
provisions.normalized_explanation: AD banks must comply with KYC, AML/CFT, tax laws, and all other regulatory provisions.
